articles.headline: Houston Astros adding J.P. Martinez, Aaron Bates to coaching staff
keyFacts: The Houston Astros are hiring coaches J.P. Martinez and Aaron Bates under new manager Brad Ausmus, sources confirmed Monday.
Martinez is reportedly replacing Josh Miller as pitching coach, while Bates joins the staff after working with the Dodgers.
The team has experienced significant turnover in its front office and coaching staff this offseason under Ausmus and general manager Randy Flores.
body: J.P. Martinez (left) and Aaron Bates are the newest additions to the Astros' coaching staff. (Getty Images)
In building out their major-league staff under new manager Brad Ausmus, the Houston Astros are hiring coaches J.P. Martinez and Aaron Bates, a person with knowledge of the additions confirmed Monday.

Martinez has worked with pitchers, including as Atlanta's bullpen coach last season and previously as a pitching coach for the Giants. Bates spent the past four seasons as co-hitting coach for the Dodgers. The Athletic first reported their impending hires.
The Astros have not announced any additions to their coaching staff under Ausmus beyond the hiring of Bobby Wilson as bench coach last week.

Last month, the Astros said they planned to retain pitching coach Josh Miller and hitting coach Victor Rodriguez from their 2026 coaching staff. However, that was before the team hired general manager Randy Flores and Ausmus, who was named manager Nov. 11 .

Miller will not return to the Astros' staff next season, people with knowledge said Monday. Martinez will reportedly replace him as pitching coach. Rodriguez's status is unclear though he was expected to return to the staff in some capacity as of Monday night.

Rodriguez served as Houston's lead hitting coach in 2026 with Anthony Iapoce as assistant hitting coach and Dan Hennigan as offensive coordinator. The Astros did not retain Iapoce after the season. Hennigan left the organization for a job at Wake Forest in August.

Martinez, 44, served as Atlanta's bullpen coach last season following five seasons on the Giants' staff as assistant pitching coach from 2021-24 and pitching coach in 2025. Prior to that, Martinez worked for six seasons in the Twins' system, including as a minor-league pitching coach and assistant coordinator.

The Astros' pitching staff ranked 24th in the majors in ERA this past season after compiling the American League's lowest ERA from 2021-25. They are poised to return the makings of a rotation led by Hunter Brown and a star closer in Josh Hader but used a franchise-record 19 different starting pitchers in 2026 and could lose several veteran relievers in free agency this offseason.

Bates spent 12 seasons in the Dodgers organization, including the past eight on their major-league staff. He was an assistant hitting coach for four years before becoming co-hitting coach. Bates also worked as the Dodgers' minor-league hitting director and as a minor-league coach.

The Dodgers parted with Bates earlier this month. Los Angeles' attempt at a third straight World Series title this year ended with an NLCS loss to the eventual champion Brewers, but its offense ranked fourth in the majors in runs scored and has finished fourth or higher each of the last four seasons.

Houston's offense ranked 13th in the majors in runs scored last season, seventh in OPS and first in home runs, led by Yordan Alvarez, who was voted the AL Most Valuable Player . It's poised to return Alvarez, Carlos Correa and Jose Altuve, among others, but may also undergo change this winter with an infield surplus and the need to address an outfield that ranked among the sport's least productive in 2026.

Turnover has already occurred in Houston's front office and field staff. The Astros opted not to retain manager Joe Espada last month, also dismissing Iapoce, assistant pitching coach Ethan Katz, catching instructor Tim Cossins, third-base coach Tony Perezchica and game planning coach Tommy Kawamura. Former bench coach Omar López was offered the chance to stay in the organization in a different role.
The Astros said last month they would retain Miller, Rodriguez, first-base coach Dave Clark and major-league field coordinator Jason Bell. Bell subsequently left for a role on the Red Sox staff .
Ausmus said after being hired that one of his first priorities would be to work with Flores on filling out the coaching staff, a process reflected in Monday's additions.

keyFacts: The Chicago Bulls defeated the Cleveland Cavaliers 122-108 on Monday following a previous loss to the Denver Nuggets.
The Bulls bench scored 48 points in the first half, setting a new franchise record and the second-most in a half since the 1997-98 play-by-play era began, per K.C. Johnson and Bulls PR.
The 5-12 Bulls will next play an away game against the Charlotte Hornets on Wednesday.

The Chicago Bulls have had a hectic stretch. In the last week, they played seven games, including Sunday, when they lost to the Denver Nuggets in overtime . However, Chicago bounced back and secured a solid 122-108 win over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday.

A major factor was their bench. The first half alone set the tone , per K.C. Johnson of The Chicago Sports Network. articles.headline: Trump faces backlash after saying he 'convinced' Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
keyFacts: Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang after Donald Trump said he convinced the board to bring him back following his resignation.
Lawmakers from both parties criticized the decision over national security concerns and Donald Trump's personal Nvidia stock investments.
Congress vowed to investigate the reinstatement, and Huang is scheduled to testify before House and Senate committees next week.
body: - Published

Nvidia has reinstated CEO Jensen Huang just days after rejecting his offer to return to the AI chipmaker - and less than two weeks after he was forced to resign over a reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy.
The company came under pressure by Donald Trump to reappoint Huang - and on Monday, the US president said he "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to bring him back.
But now both Trump and Nvidia are facing bipartisan backlash from lawmakers, just as Huang is due to testify before Congress next week.
The CEO's comeback helped end a week-long losing streak in US stocks that left the S&P 500 in correction territory, and added nearly $1 trillion to Nvidia's market value.
Stock prices for Nvidia fell sharply after Huang stepped down, but jumped by 31% after he was reappointed on Monday - adding about $1tn to the company's market value.
But Nvidia's closing price was still down slightly from its Friday morning opening price.
As Asian stock markets opened, Nvidia racked up more gains and helped lift other share prices across the tech sector.

Board Chairman Harvey C Jones said in a statement earlier in the day: "The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers."
The board said it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.
It was only last Tuesday that the board explicitly said it did not intend to reinstate him.
Huang resigned from Nvidia on 12 November following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman, Alice Huang, who was alleged to have ties to Chinese intelligence.
On Monday, the US Commerce Department announced it was preparing to blacklist Megaspeed, the Singapore-based Nvidia customer where Alice Huang was CEO.

In a brief interview with CNBC on Monday, Trump said he had spoken to Nvidia's board of directors and "convinced" them to bring back Huang. Trump praised the Nvidia board for acting "really responsibly" in reinstating the CEO.
"They did ask for assurance on the national security threat," Trump said. "And we gave them assurances at least with everything we know. And we know a lot."
"People say, is it a threat to have him? No, it's a threat to lose him," the president added.
The president was asked whether Nvidia stock losses after Huang resigned last week had influenced his decision to personally intervene.
"Probably so," Trump said.
Congress vows to investigate Nvidia and the Trump administration's role
The head of the International Association for Safe and Ethical AI told the BBC that the Nvidia board must have been under "enormous pressure" from the White House to reinstate Huang.
Prof Stuart Russell, who is professor of computer science at UC Berkeley, said the stock price of Nvidia and similar firms has been a major factor in "underpinning US economic growth for years".
"I assume the White House was worried that the markets would go down a lot further in the next few weeks unless they go him back in," he says.
Trump's vocal backing of Huang comes despite the concerns of US lawmakers, including some Republicans, over the CEO's affair and Nvidia's compliance with US export controls.

Hakeem Jeffries, who is expected to lead the House of Representatives as Speaker when Democrats take control in January called the decision to reinstate Huang "indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible" and vowed that Congress will conduct "a swift, thorough and wide-ranging investigation".

"We will not allow America's national security to be sold out by the Trump Administration for personal financial gain," he said, echoing many lawmakers on Monday who said that Congress must pass strong export control legislation.
Huang is scheduled to appear before Congress for a closed-door interview with three House committees on 1 December. Two days later, he has been asked to testify before the Senate banking committee.
Senator Elizabeth Warren, who is set to be chairwoman of the Senate Banking Committee once Democrats take control of the chamber in January, said in a statement that the reinstatement was "reckless".
"The Trump Administration also needs to explain to Congress what 'input' was given and by which senior officials in the United States government to support his reinstatement," she also said.
Republicans, too, called for answers.

"Nvidia should have moved on without Huang and ignored the administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang," said Republican Representative Don Bacon, who chairs a House subcommittee on cyber security.
"We cannot say we want to win the AI race and then give China our best technology. We need sunlight on who is responsible."

The chair of the Senate's select committee on intelligence, Republican Tom Cotton said: "The controversy with Nvidia and Megaspeed is just the tip of the iceberg, and it's not resolved because Jensen Huang has his job back."
Trump's personal Nvidia investments

Since returning last year to the White House, Trump has amassed a significant level of investment in Nvidia. Recent financial disclosures show he purchased $265,000 in its stock and sold as much as $15,000 worth of shares in September.

A BBC review of his government financial disclosures for the last two years shows he purchased shares of Nvidia stock worth between $23m and $86m (Â£18m and Â£66m). And he has bought Nvidia stock 85 separate times through a number of investment accounts.
The value of those holdings would have been affected by the recent fall in Nvidia's stock price amid Huang's exit.
Trump has also sold some of his stake in Nvidia since returning to the presidency. Over 19 sales, Trump gained between $3.5m and $10.2m, according to his government disclosures.
The BBC has contacted the White House.

Both Trump and White House have repeatedly rejected assertions that he has profited from the presidency. The president has said "everybody" was making money from rising stocks and he does not make decisions related to his investment accounts.
The White House has emphasised that Trump has placed his businesses in a trust managed by his sons.
With additional reporting from Brandon Drenon and Rachel Clun

articles.headline: 2026 NFL playoff picture, standings: 49ers reign over NFC, Jaguars slip in AFC, wild-card battles heat up
keyFacts: As Week 12 approaches, all seven playoff seeds in both the AFC and NFC remain open as teams compete for postseason position.
The San Francisco 49ers lead the NFC playoff picture following a dominant performance, while the Buffalo Bills and Denver Broncos hold top spots in the AFC.
Several division leaders, including the Jacksonville Jaguars and Cincinnati Bengals, experienced setbacks in Week 11 that impacted their playoff seeding.
body: If there is any truth to the adage that the NFL season does not truly start until Thanksgiving, then now is the time to start taking the playoff race seriously. As the calendar turns to Week 12 and a loaded holiday slate, all seven seeds in both conferences are up for grabs, and there are a number of teams beyond the current cut line that could not only make their way into the bracket but also compete for home-field advantage in the postseason.

Anyone that aims to lock up a first-round bye in the NFC has to get through the San Francisco 49ers, which is a daunting task considering how dominant they appeared on the Week 11 edition of "Sunday Night Football."

And in the AFC, the Jacksonville Jaguars learned a difficult lesson on Sunday about how slim the margins are in the race for the No. 1 seed when they suffered a costly setback against the New York Giants.
With seven weeks of regular-season action to go, here is a snapshot of the playoff picture in both NFL conferences.
AFC standings, playoff picture
- Buffalo Bills (9-1)
- Denver Broncos (8-2)
- Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3)
- Cincinnati Bengals (7-3)
- Kansas City Chiefs (8-2)
- Cleveland Browns (6-4)
- Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4)
1. Buffalo Bills (9-1)
Remaining schedule: vs. Chiefs, at Patriots, at Packers, vs. Bears, at Broncos, at Dolphins, vs. Jets

The only blemish on the Bills' resume is a three-point divisional loss to the Patriots, but that should not come back to bite them in the AFC East race as they hold a commanding four-game lead. It does make them vulnerable in the battle for the conference's No. 1 seed, though. The schedule is about to stiffen up following a four-game stretch in which Josh Allen feasted on beleaguered opponents and the defense corrected its early-season woes by allowing no more than 12 points in any of those contests.
2. Denver Broncos (8-2)
Remaining schedule: at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers

That the Broncos fended off Fernando Mendoza and the Raiders was critical for Denver's chances of winning the AFC West. Sean Payton's squad holds a tiebreaker over the Chiefs thanks to their higher win percentage against common opponents. It was a rare win by double digits for a team that is prolific at squeaking out victories by a one-score margin and increased the win streak to six games, which is tied for the longest in the conference.
3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3)
Remaining schedule: vs. Titans, at Bears, vs. Steelers, at Texans, at Cowboys, vs. Commanders, at Colts

Trevor Lawrence endured uncharacteristic struggles in a loss to the Giants that halted the Jaguars' momentum. In each of their previous four games, they scored at least 31 points. They managed only 18 against New York. The AFC South is still theirs by a three-game margin, so the defeat only has implications for seeding inside the top four. This team went all-in at the trade deadline and would thus figure to be disappointed with anything less than the No. 1 seed, but so long as everything comes together in the postseason, one loss in Week 11 will not haunt them.
4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-3)
Remaining schedule: vs. Saints, at Browns, vs. Chiefs, at Panthers, at Colts, vs. Ravens, vs. Browns

Monday's last-second loss to the Commanders did not drop the Bengals out of first place in the AFC North, but they slipped behind the Jaguars on a tiebreaker after their head-to-head defeat earlier in the season. Cincinnati is fortunate that none of the other teams in its division picked up a win in Week 11.
5. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2)
Remaining schedule: at Bills, at Rams, at Bengals, vs. Patriots, vs. 49ers, at Chargers, vs. Raiders

The battle with the Broncos to secure home-field advantage in the Wild Card round could come down to the last week of the season. The Chiefs have done nearly everything they can to lock up one of those prized seeds yet find themselves on the outside looking in due to Denver's tiebreaker in the division. Kansas City has been mauling overmatched opponents of late and needs that to translate to the much stiffer competition that lies ahead over the next five weeks.
6. Cleveland Browns (6-4)
Remaining schedule: vs. Raiders, vs. Bengals, vs. Falcons, at Giants, at Ravens, vs. Colts, at Bengals

The Browns hold a tiebreaker over the Steelers for the No. 6 seed because of their divisional win percentage. They split the regular-season series with Pittsburgh and won their only other AFC North contest, 13-10, over the Baltimore Ravens. Among the more pleasant surprises of the entire NFL season is what first-year coach Todd Monken continues to achieve in turning Deshaun Watson back into a serviceable starting quarterback and how defensive coordinator Mike Rutenberg constructed a competitive group following the offseason Myles Garrett trade.
7. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4)
Remaining schedule: vs. Broncos, vs. Texans, at Jaguars, vs. Ravens, vs. Panthers, at Titans, at Ravens

It was only three weeks ago that the Steelers held sole possession of the AFC North lead. Everything since then has been a disaster. They no-showed a week ago in a primetime loss to the Bengals and, on Sunday, were on the wrong side of the Eagles, who snapped a seven-game losing streak. That in-state loss marked a new low for the 2026 Steelers. They remain on the right side of the postseason cut line, but it is a tenuous position.
In the hunt

No team outside the top seven is better than 5-5, and that lone .500 team will be without its quarterback until further notice. The Patriots (5-5) would be the top contender to move up the ladder if Drake Maye were healthy, but in his absence, the door is open for teams a little further down. That includes the Texans (4-6), who could become just the second team in NFL history to start a season 0-4 and reach the playoffs. The pickings are slim behind them, as the Ravens (4-7) and Raiders (4-7) are operating with a backup quarterback and rookie signal-caller, respectively.
NFC standings, playoff picture
- San Francisco 49ers (9-1)
- Detroit Lions (8-2)
- New York Giants (6-3-1)
- Carolina Panthers (5-5)
- Chicago Bears (8-2)
- Minnesota Vikings (7-3)
- Green Bay Packers (6-4)
1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1)
Remaining schedule: vs. Seahawks, at Giants, vs. Rams, at Chargers, at Chiefs, vs. Eagles, at Cardinals

If a decisive win over a fellow championship contender and a 35-point outburst against the NFL's top defense does not cement the 49ers as Super Bowl favorites, then nothing will. San Francisco is undoubtedly the team to beat. Mike Evans' return in the Mexico City Game injected even more life into the offense and gives Kyle Shanahan yet another weapon to deploy in the weeks to come as he unleashes an unstoppable attack on the rest of the league. The NFC is the 49ers' to lose.
2. Detroit Lions (8-2)
Remaining schedule: vs. Bears, at Falcons, vs. Titans, at Vikings, vs. Giants, at Bears, at Packers

The Lions hold a tiebreaker over the Bears for the NFC North lead with the greater win percentage in division games, but that will not matter in just a few days when the head-to-head result between the two on Thanksgiving determines who has the inside track to home-field advantage in the Wild Card round. Detroit, as it stands, is the top threat to the 49ers at the top of the conference and owns the kind of offensive star power it would take to unseat them from the NFC's catbird seat should they square off in the postseason.
3. New York Giants (6-3-1)
Remaining schedule: at Colts, vs. 49ers, at Seahawks, vs. Browns, at Lions, at Cowboys, vs. Eagles

The Giants passed their biggest test of the year on Sunday when they took down the Jaguars in a colossal 23-18 victory. Every other win on their ledger is against a sub-.500 team, so the Week 11 triumph was by far the most impressive and legitimized their division lead. They remain the only NFC East team with a winning record and own a defense that seems capable of keeping them in control of their own destiny in the hunt for a top-four playoff seed.
4. Carolina Panthers (5-5)
Remaining schedule: at Buccaneers, at Vikings, vs. Saints, vs. Bengals, at Steelers, vs. Seahawks, vs. Falcons

Such is the state of the NFC South that the Panthers are merely .500 yet own a two-game lead over the rest of the division. Every other team is 3-7. There exists a realistic path for Carolina to move up to the No. 3 seed since the NFC East is nearly as weak as their own division, but that is probably the ceiling. Back-to-back wins and Chuba Hubbard's emergence as a prominent bell-cow running back have the Panthers trending the right way.
5. Chicago Bears (8-2)
Remaining schedule: at Lions, vs. Jaguars, at Dolphins, at Bills, vs. Packers, at Lions, at Vikings

The Jeffery Simmons effect is obvious. The Bears are unbeaten since they traded for the superstar defensive tackle, and he came through with three sacks on Sunday to match a career high and aid Chicago in defeating the Saints, 21-13. Simmons' presence will be of the utmost importance next week against the Lions' incredible rushing attack and the following week when the Bears take on Jacksonville in an intra-conference blockbuster.
6. Minnesota Vikings (7-3)
Remaining schedule: vs. Falcons, vs. Panthers, at Patriots, vs. Lions, vs. Commanders, at Jets, vs. Bears

Is it time to be concerned about the Vikings? All of a sudden, Minnesota has lost three of its last four games. Sure, the "Sunday Night Football" disaster can be chalked up to playing against a stellar offense in a not-even-remotely-neutral environment in Mexico City. But the Vikings are going to have to beat teams of the 49ers' caliber to get to the mountaintop, and they have done nothing but lose to them over the last month. The elite defense will only take them so far, and on days like Sunday when not even that group shows up, things can get really bleak.
7. Green Bay Packers (6-4)
Remaining schedule: at Rams, at Saints, vs. Bills, vs. Dolphins, at Bears, vs. Texans, vs. Lions

The NFC North is what most expected the NFC West to be in that it could send three or four teams to the postseason. There is a battle between the two divisions for the final wild card spot. The Seahawks and Rams are both 6-4, so Seattle holds the tiebreaker based on win percentage in division games. But the Packers then hold a tiebreaker over Seattle due to their conference win percentage.
In the hunt

The NFC North and NFC West will cannibalize themselves to an extent, which may open the door for the Cowboys (5-6) or even the Commanders (4-5-1) to sneak their way into the No. 7 seed. But there is a chasm between them and the teams ahead of them in terms of overall team quality. The Seahawks (6-4) and Rams (6-4) are both more complete squads. There might only be room for one of them to get into the bracket, though, which would be a surprise given the former's status as the reigning champion and the latter's preseason outlook as the Super Bowl favorite.

articles.headline: India: Report warns of deepening authoritarianism under Modi
keyFacts: A Human Rights Watch report concluded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government has systematically weakened India's democratic institutions.
The watchdog said the government is suppressing opposition, weaponizing investigative agencies, and eroding the rule of law.
Human Rights Watch urged allies to press Modi's government, which has not yet commented on the findings.
body: What you need to know
- Report warns against India's democratic backsliding under Prime Minister Narendra Modi
- Man injures nine police officer with knife, held after several gunshots
Here are the biggest headlines from India on Tuesday, November 24:
India deepens authoritarian slide under Modi — Report

Prime Minister Modi's Hindu nationalist government has "systematically weakened" institutions meant to protect human rights and democratic freedoms, a scathing new report by Human Rights Watch concluded.

In a 95-page report titled 'So What's This Democracy We're Talking About?: Modi's Authoritarian Playbook in India,' the watchdog found that the right-wing Bharatiya Janata Party-led (BJP) government is undermining parliamentary procedures, suppressing opposition and weaponzing investigative agencies for political ends.
It also found that the government has weakened constitutional and statutory bodies meant to protect democratic freedoms and the rights of the people.
'Authoritarian playbook'

"Over the past decade, the Modi government has been hollowing out India’s independent institutions that are critical to checking executive power and protecting civil liberties," said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch.

"The government has eroded the rule of law and promoted Hindu majoritarianism, rolling back human rights protections, undermining the rights of marginalized communities, and deepening India's authoritarian slide."

The report further claimed the Election Commission of India and the Supreme Court — both independent bodies — failed to uphold fundamental freedoms, pointing to the elimination of millions of voter names from India's electoral rolls in a controversial exercise.
"The Modi administration's actions over the past decade are not isolated institutional failures but mutually reinforcing elements of an authoritarian playbook," Human Rights Watch said.
"India's allies should press the Modi government to end its assault on independent institutions and restore checks on executive power," Pearson said.
The BJP or Modi's government is yet to comment on the report which was published Tuesday morning. However, both have dismissed similar criticisms in the past.
Welcome to our coverage
Hello! and welcome to DW's India blog.
This is Mahima Kapoor reporting from Studio Delhi. Even as the temperature is fast dropping in the national capital, Prime Minister Narendra Modi is facing a different kind of heat.

A new report by Human Rights Watch has raised concerns over India's deteriorating democratic institutions and growing authoritarianism under his leadership, putting the government's record on rights and freedoms back in the spotlight.

Incidentally, hours before the report was published, one of the leaders of India's cockroach movement claimed he was not allowed to board his overnight flight to the UK to deliver speeches at the universities of Oxford, Cambridge and Edinburgh and the London School of Economics.
In other news, a Delhi man reportedly injured nine police men during a stabbing spree after he was called in to a police station over a familial dispute.
Stay tuned for all of this and more!

articles.headline: NFL playoff picture: Updated AFC, NFC standings after Week 11 of 2026 season
keyFacts: The Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers hold the top seeds in the AFC and NFC respectively after Week 11 of the 2026 season.
The Denver Broncos and Kansas City both hold 8-2 records in the AFC West, with the Broncos leading due to conference record tiebreakers.
The Carolina Panthers hold a two-game lead in the NFC South division standings following a home win against the Baltimore Ravens.
body: What if the 2026 NFL regular season ended after Week 11? Which teams would make the playoffs, from the highest seeds to the lowest wild cards in both the NFC and AFC? Which teams would be on the outside looking in, with their focus turning more toward the 2027 offseason?
Here's an updated look at the race to get into the tournament ahead of Super Bowl 61 in Los Angeles on Feb. 14:
MORE: Week 12 power rankings
NFL playoff picture after Week 11
Imagn Images via Reuters Connect
AFC
1. Buffalo Bills 9-1 (first place, AFC East)

The Bills don't need to worry about fading New England in the division race as they take the crown back easily, with the goal now of finishing ahead of top AFC contenders to secure home-field advantage and the bye.
2. Denver Broncos 8-2 (first place, AFC West)

The Broncos jumped here by beating the Raiders and matching the Chiefs' division record of 3-1 through four games in AFC West play. With the common-games tiebreaker not eligible, the Broncos get here by having a better conference record (6-1 vs. 4-1).
3. Jacksonville Jaguars 7-3 (first place, AFC South)

The Jaguars saw their three-game winning streak end against the Giants in ugly fashion, but they still don't need to worry about repeating in the division with a commanding three-game lead over the Texans with only seven games left. But they lost ground to the Bills and the Broncos.
4. Cincinnati Bengals 7-3 (first place, AFC North)

The Bengals still lead the division by a game over the Steelers after beating that team last week to even the season series. Unfortunately, Cincinnati suffered a rough upset loss at Washington on Monday night to fall back to this seed.
5. Kansas City Chiefs 8-2 (first place, AFC West)

The Chiefs, who split the season series with the second-place Broncos, lost the lead in the division for now, despite beating the Cardinals. The Chiefs will go to the Bills next on Thursday, while the Broncos play at the Steelers on Friday.
6. Cleveland Browns 6-4 (third place, AFC North)
The Browns are in a surprise final wild-card spot going into their Week 11 bye. They will have a huge home game in Week 12, trying to stay in position, on Sunday night vs. the Raiders.
7. Pittsburgh Steelers 6-4 (second place, AFC North)
The Steelers lost as favorites on the road Philadelphia, dropping them further back of the Bengals and also pushing them below the Browns for losing the division record tiebreaker (2-1 vs. 2-2).
Who's in the hunt?
8. New England Patriots (5-5)
9. Houston Texans (4-6)
10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-7)
11. Baltimore Ravens (4-7)

The Browns and Steelers have a one-game lead over the Patriots and a two-game lead over the Texans. Anybody from this group can sneak into the playoffs with a hot final two months. The Ravens missed a big chance with their loss at Carolina.
Who's left?
12. New York Jets (3-8)
13. Indianapolis Colts (3-8)
14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-9)
15. Tennessee Titans (1-9)
16. Miami Dolphins (1-9)

With eight losses, three of these teams have no margin for error if they hope to finish above .500, as it will likely take more than nine wins to make the AFC playoffs. The Dolphins and the Titans are set to be eliminated.
NFC
IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect
1. San Francisco 49ers 9-1 (first place, NFC West)

The 49ers are well positioned to take back the division with a strong three-game lead over both the Seahawks and Rams, with road wins against both teams. After ripping the Vikings on Sunday night, they have a favorable schedule to keep the top seed that comes with home-field advantage and the lone bye.
2. Detroit Lions 8-2 (first place, NFC North)

The Lions are up on the same-record Bears after Week 11 with the division-record tiebreaker (2-0 vs. 0-2) and now a full game up on the Vikings. They need to hope their defense keeps holding up without Aidan Hutchinson, just like it did against the Buccaneers.
3. New York Giants 6-3-1 (first place, NFC East)

The Giants still have a two-game lead over the Cowboys after they beat the Jaguars in Week 12. They are feeling much better about their chances to take the division in the first year under John Harbaugh.
4. Carolina Panthers 5-5 (first place, NFC South)

articles.headline: Fantasy Baseball Offseason Tracker: Trevor Rogers' deal with Cubs underscores his upside
keyFacts: Trevor Rogers signed a five-year, $120 million contract with the Chicago Cubs, which analysts note highlights his underlying pitching upside.
Tarik Skubal signed a nine-year, $450 million contract with the New York Mets, marking the largest contract ever for a pitcher.
Several players changed teams or accepted qualifying offers ahead of an anticipated lockout, impacting their fantasy baseball outlooks.
body: A lockout may be coming, but nobody told the hot stove. It's already burning bright with even the biggest prize, two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal, coming off the market.

Once the lockout becomes official, the signings -- and all other transactions -- will cease, but those that occur before then will still count toward the date when baseball is allowed to resume. So we'd better document them all here, just like any other offseason, breaking down their impact for Fantasy Baseball.

That's what Scott White and Chris Towers intend to do over the next few weeks, at least, before everything goes quiet. They'll eventually pick up where they left off when the hot stove heats up again in ... March? Hopefully not much later than that.
Whatever the timeline, you'll want this page bookmarked so you can get the first word on everything that happens.
Trevor Rogers signs with Cubs

Maybe you thought Sonny Gray's two-year, $55 million deal with the Twins was too little. Maybe you thought Tarik Skubal's nine-year, $450 million deal with the Mets was too much. Does that make Rogers' five-year, $120 million deal with the Cubs just right? For me, maybe, since I rank him 36th at starting pitcher, but early ADP has him going only 53rd, behind the likes of Nick Pivetta and Christian Scott. It's clear, then, that Fantasy Baseballers, at least the kind that participate in November NFBC drafts, don't regard Rogers as highly as the game at large does. A big reason for that, I think, is that he had an ERA over 4.00 in 2026, which most Roto rating systems regard as an albatross around a pitcher's neck, but perhaps a better indicator of the way he pitched was his 3.45 FIP.

Even that doesn't entirely do him justice. He has a 3.16 ERA, 1.07 WHIP and 8.4 K/9 in 48 starts over the past two seasons and had a 2.90 ERA, 1.03 WHIP and 8.9 K/9 over his final 20 starts in 2026. Sure, he was bad early on -- so much that his breakthrough 2025 was written off as a fluke in some corners -- but I suspect that a bout with the flu -- one so severe that it landed him on the IL for two weeks in April and May -- also had a deleterious effect on his mechanics. Once he got them sorted out, he was a top-of-the-rotation arm again, and that's how he spent the majority of his 2026. It doesn't hurt either that the Cubs ranked a distant No. 1 in defensive runs saved last year. The Orioles, by comparison, were middle of the pack. Let this be your reminder not to underrate Rogers in drafts, as so many are. --Scott White
Tarik Skubal signs with Mets

At nine years, $450 million, Skubal's contract with the Mets is the biggest ever for a pitcher, bettering the $325 million deal that the Dodgers gave Yoshinobu Yamamoto prior to the 2024 season. So does it confirm he's the SP1 for 2027, ahead of even Jacob Misiorowski? There's at least a case for it, even with the Mets' reputation for being the Wile E. Coyote of baseball teams, by which I mean doomed to see every state-of-the-art purchase blow up in their face. For more, check out my full-length article. --Scott White
Royce Lewis traded to Dodgers

At first glance, this looks like the nail in the coffin for a player whose Fantasy value has already been in free fall, but Lewis can play all over the diamond and the Dodgers have no shortage of geriatric players. He may not play as consistently as he did with the Twins, but between spelling Max Muncy at third base, spelling Freddie Freeman at first base, and filling in for whatever injury pops up, Lewis should play enough to be of some use in Rotisserie leagues, with their larger lineups.

And that's all you should have been counting on anyway with the way his numbers have trended since 2024. He made such a splash to begin his career that it seemed like only injuries would hold him back, but he's shown himself to be just a .230 hitter over the past three years. Maybe with consistent playing time, he could eke out 20 homers, particularly now that he's in a more favorable venue for him, but again, his playing time is about to be less consistent, not more. --Scott White
Maikel Garcia traded to Mariners

This is a trade that makes a ton of sense for real-life baseball but might be a disaster for Fantasy. The Mariners got -0.5 WAR from their third basemen in 2026, per FanGraphs, and Garcia represents a significant upgrade from that. As recently as 2025, put up a .286/.351/.449 line and was a borderline elite Fantasy option as a result.

Unfortunately for our purposes, this trade makes it a lot less likely he'll live up to that level of play in 2027. Kauffman Stadium in Kansas City suppresses homers but is generally a pretty good offensive environment, sporting the seventh-best park factor for hitters, per BaseballSavant.com. T-Mobile Park in Seattle? It's the worst hitter's park in baseball by a pretty wide margin, though how that impacts each individual hitter often varies. Randy Arozarena more or less held serve in his time in Seattle, while someone like Eugenio Suarez struggled mightily in both stints there. It's something about the way hitters see the ball and how the humid, often chilly atmosphere affects batted balls' trajectories. There just isn't another offensive environment in baseball quite like T-Mobile Park, and it generally serves as a drag on offense across the board.

If Garcia can hit like he did in 2025, he'll still be very fantasy-relevant, however. That season saw Garcia max out his power, bumping his average exit velocity to 91.3 mph, while also increasing his launch angle, allowing him to tap into far more of that power than ever before. That he did it without sacrificing his superlative contact skills made for a very strong package. But he gave back nearly all of those improvements in 2026 and returned to being a roughly average hitter. He struggled while playing through injuries to his left hand and wrist before eventually going on the IL for nearly two months, then struggled with hamstring issues late in the season. If the injuries explain his struggles, then betting on a bounceback makes sense, even in Seattle.

But 2025 might have just been a career year, and the move to T-Mobile Park makes it even less likely he'll get back to that level. Garcia's price has already slipped to 169.4 in early NFBC drafts, but I'd expect it to drop even farther after this. He's a fringe starting-caliber third baseman for Fantasy, and I'd take at least Curtis Mead and Isaac Paredes ahead of him, among players with a current lower ADP. --Chris Towers
Bryce Miller traded to the Royals

While Maikel Garcia is going to the worst hitter's park in the league, Miller suffers from the opposite move, exiting one of the best pitching environments in the league. It's one he has specifically benefited from, sporting a career 3.49 ERA at home compared to a 4.63 ERA on the road. It would be overly simplistic to say he has lost whatever Fantasy relevance he had with this move, but it might not end up wrong.

To add some nuance, I think Miller can be a good pitcher in any offensive environment; he just hasn't been for long. He's had stretches across different seasons where he has looked like an ace, but he never manages to sustain it. He has pitched through various elbow issues over the years, but when he is right, he rides a high-vert, high-velo fastball to very good results. Let's not forget that he started the 2026 season with a 1.71 ERA and 10.6 K/9 in his first eight starts, but then he tried pitching through a lat issue and wasn't the same. Still, it was another reminder of how good he can be at his best. Given the inconsistency and the park downgrade, Miller should continue to see his price fall. He's down to 266.3 in those early NFBC drafts and should probably just be a reserve round dart throw now that he's with the Royals. --Chris Towers
Sonny Gray signs with the Twins

It's not the first place I would have bet on Gray signing, but the Twins have made it clear since the most recent trade deadline that they aren't looking to rebuild. The deal is officially for one year but includes a 2028 player option for the 37-year-old Gray, meaning the Twins will either be happy about getting one great season out of him or will be looking at a fairly onerous (but short!) deal for 2028. It's a tradeoff worth making for a team like the Twins, who have talent in the rotation but little in the way of sure things, either from a performance or a health perspective. Gray is seemingly a different type of pitcher every season, but from a real-life perspective, it's easy to see the appeal in employing him: He has made at least 24 starts in every season since 2017 (minus the shortened 2020 season) and has had an ERA over 4.00 just twice in his past eight seasons.

From a Fantasy perspective, his value is a little less clear. He had an excellent 2026 season that saw him take advantage of an elite Red Sox defense to put up a 2.72 ERA. It did, however, come with a huge decrease in his strikeout rate, and that came after two seasons with a combined ERA of 4.07. He's almost always a must-start pitcher, but it often feels like you can't fully trust him. Of course, with an ADP around 150 in early drafts, it doesn't really matter if you can fully trust him. Just roll him out there, hope the ERA is closer to 3.50 than 4.00 and don't overthink it. He's a nice rotation filler as long as you don't expect him to be an ace. --Chris Towers
David Bednar accepts Yankees' qualifying offer

This one comes as a mild surprise and makes me wonder if Bednar just really wanted to stay with a team that wasn't willing to give him a multi-year commitment. He's a 32-year-old closer, and while he has mostly been a very good one over the past six seasons, there have been enough bumps in the road along the way to make the risk for Bednar pretty obvious. But from a Fantasy perspective, Bednar safely looks like a top-12 closer now that he's returning to the Yankees. His strikeout rate regressed in 2026, but his swinging-strike rate was actually higher than the previous season, and none of his underlying metrics otherwise really tell the story of a pitcher in decline. He's somewhere shy of the elite tier of closers for Fantasy, but he's good enough (and secure enough in his role for a good team) to be worth drafting as your primary source of saves. --Chris Towers
Ryan Jeffers accepts Twins' qualifying offer

It was a mild surprise to see the Twins extend Jeffers the qualifying offer, but it's not a surprise to see him accept it. Jeffers is a solid starting catcher -- good enough to be worth a fair share of playing time from the DH spot but he isn't the kind of player who was likely looking at a bunch of $50-plus million offers either. It's why taking the $23.2 million qualifying offer (and becoming the highest-paid catcher in baseball by annual value!) makes some sense here.

It also keeps the status quo in line for Jeffers. He'll play a decent amount and be reasonably productive when he's out there, but Jeffers' apparent breakout in the first half of 2026 proved unsustainable as he settled in more or less where we've come to expect him to be. He's a good hitter for a catcher, but given the strength of the position, he's more of a solid No. 2 catcher option than a true difference maker. That's nice to have around when it comes at the cost of a pick around 200th overall, as it should in most leagues. --Chris Towers
Dustin May signs with White Sox

There might be some sticker shock here – "$50 million for a career 4.12 ERA pitcher who has never thrown 150 innings in a season?" – but that's just the market rate for pitchers who reach free agency with their arms attached. May has been viewed as someone with a lot of upside over the years, but I think we're past that point after he showed little more than mid-rotation abilities in two seasons split between the Dodgers, Red Sox, and Brewers. He's a nice rotation filler for the White Sox, but unless something drastic happens to change his profile, he's a better source of GIFs than Fantasy production at this point in his career. --Chris Towers
Jake Bauers signs with Red Sox

After a surprise breakthrough season in which the underlying data was as sparkling as the top-line production, the biggest concern for Bauers was whether he'd sign with an organization that would help or hinder his follow-up campaign. By most outward indicators, he chose poorly. Sure, he'll be thrilled to get $58 million over the next four years, but his expected home run number at Fenway Park, with its deep right field fence, was only 18, tied for worst among all 30 venues.

He also joins a crowd of five players for four spots -- that is, unless (or until?) the Red Sox trade Jarren Duran. Even if Bauers himself isn't the one to sacrifice at-bats because of it (and look, he's no sure thing, for as good as he was in 2026), the potential impact on Willson Contreras, Roman Anthony, Wilyer Abreu and Duran makes his arrival a net negative for Fantasy. Bottom line is that this signing only amplifies the natural skepticism for a late-career breakout and explains why Bauers barely ranks inside my top 30 outfielders. --Scott White
Emilio Pagan signs with Tigers

The Tigers weren't willing to pay Kenley Jansen $12 million to be their closer, declining his option at the start of the offseason, and then turned around and signed Pagan for about the same amount. Probably safe to assume, then, he's their new closer after serving in the same capacity for the Reds the past two years. His 2026 performance was solid overall, but he was particularly dominant after returning from an early hamstring injury, delivering a 1.88 ERA, 0.84 WHIP and 10.7 K/9 over his final 30 appearances. The home run issues that prevented him from becoming a closer earlier in his career remain acute. Still, if he was able to navigate the past two years in Cincinnati with them, for as homer-friendly as that environment is, he should be able to do the same in Detroit. He'll be a budget-friendly RP2 on Draft Day. --Scott White
Evan Phillips signs with the Braves

The first multi-year signing of the offseason wasn't a headline name, and Phillips seems likely to open the season as the setup man behind Robert Suarez with his new squad. But Phillips is being paid over $10 million a year on a three-year deal, which is a decent-sized investment for a non-closer and reflects the upside he once showed in a high-leverage role. He came back from his June 2025 Tommy John surgery to pitch effectively for the Dodgers in 2026, posting a 3.46 ERA over 26 innings. While the underlying data isn't quite as promising, he still missed a ton of bats and had good control. The velocity also bounced all the way back and then some, past pre-injury levels.

Assuming the Braves don't bring back Raisel Iglesias, Suarez is locked in as the closer coming off a 1.06 ERA, but seeing as he missed three months of the 2026 season with elbow discomfort, there's a non-zero chance Phillips figures into the ninth-inning situation at some point in 2027. He's not necessarily a name you need to know for Draft Day in most leagues, but Phillips could be very relevant in 2027 if things go sideways for Suarez in the way they so often do for pitchers in their mid-30s. --Chris Towers

articles.headline: Army proceeding with lead detonation on Wednesday
keyFacts: The Army is proceeding with detonating lead-containing munitions in Iowa on Wednesday.
President Trump added uncertainty to the controversy on Monday.
Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle stated the removal is coordinated with state, local, and federal authorities.
body: The Army is going ahead with detonating lead-containing munitions in Iowa on Wednesday after President Trump threw additional uncertainty into the controversy on Monday. “We are proceeding with the controlled removal in full coordination with all state, local and federal authorities, because the safety of Iowa’s citizens comes first,” said acting Army Secretary Adam Telle…

articles.headline: Army plans Wednesday detonation of unstable lead azide in Iowa
keyFacts: The U.S. Army plans to detonate five tons of unstable lead azide explosive in Middletown, Iowa, on Wednesday morning.
A federal appeals court cleared the detonation after environmental groups filed a lawsuit over safety and public notice concerns.
Officials said the 68 barrels of degraded lead azide cannot be relocated because the material is unstable.
body: Acting Army Secretary Adam Telle on Monday said the branch will move forward with detonating unstable lead explosive in Iowa on Wednesday after a federal appeals court, as well as Gov. Kim Reynolds (R-IA) and Gov.-elect Rob Sand (D-IA), gave the green light.

The 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals handed down its ruling just hours before Telle’s announcement, allowing the Army to proceed with detonating 5 tons of degraded lead azide at a World War II-era ammunition plant in Middletown.

“This is a consensus decision,” Telle said. “Every expert agency agrees, and both Iowa’s current and incoming Governors say the call belongs to the experts. We are proceeding with the controlled removal in full coordination with all state, local and federal authorities, because the safety of Iowa’s citizens comes first.”

Approval for the detonation faced several obstacles, including the lawsuit cited by Telle. Earthjustice, a nonprofit environmental law organization, sued in the federal court of appeals on behalf of the Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club Iowa Chapter. The groups argued that the Environmental Protection Agency did not require the Army to consider safer treatment alternatives, that the permit conditions do not adequately protect human health, and that the Army gave inadequate public notice.
APPEALS COURT CLEARS WAY FOR ARMY TO DETONATE UNSTABLE LEAD EXPLOSIVES IN IOWA

The detonation, originally scheduled for Friday, was postponed amid legal challenges, unfavorable weather conditions, and intervention from President Donald Trump, who said the Army should not proceed without the approval of both the court and Sand, who has not yet assumed the gubernatorial office.
Sand’s objection stemmed from feelings that the public was not well informed on the decision to move forward with the detonation.
On Monday evening, the court ultimately ruled the EPA has taken the appropriate steps to mitigate harm, including implementing adequate safeguards to prevent lead exposure to communities.
Telle said Sand ultimately agreed “based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago and have been on the ground in Middletown for weeks.”
Additionally, Telle noted the steps taken to ensure the detonation is done safely, including consulting several agencies.
IOWA LEAD EXPLOSION: HOW DID WE GET HERE?

“It is the unanimous judgement of our people — the Army, Navy, EPA, ATF, FBI, DARPA, DoE, CDC, HHS, FEMA and every other agency involved — that the Army should proceed with an extensively mitigated, carefully controlled detonation, which will occur this Wednesday morning, as previously scheduled, based on forecast wind conditions,” he said.

There are 68 barrels of degraded lead azide at the Middletown site that will be detonated on Wednesday, which officials say cannot be relocated for detonation elsewhere because the material is unstable.

articles.headline: China’s second-richest man’s deal to drain California town’s water triggers outrage: ‘Don’t sell out your nation’
keyFacts: Fairfield City Council approved a 15-year deal supplying up to 2.2 million daily gallons of water to Chinese-owned Streamfill Packers.
Former Mayor Catherine Moy requested a federal national security review over the facility's proximity to Travis Air Force Base.
Fairfield announced Ocean West Capital Partners acquired the property to lease to Streamfill, which reportedly plans to invest over $200 million.
body: Ex-Fairfield Mayor Catherine “Cat” Moy is pressing the Treasury Department and Democratic Rep. John Garamendi to intervene after Fairfield officials approved a deal last week to supply up to 2.2 million gallons of city water a day to Streamfill Packers, a subsidiary of Chinese beverage giant Nongfu Spring.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

In emails sent Nov. 18 and obtained by the California Post, Moy called for a national security review of the site — a former Anheuser-Busch brewery just seven miles from Travis Air Force Base — and urged Garamendi to help prevent operations from starting before federal officials complete a review.
Advertisement

Moy, who resigned in June, wrote to the U.S. Department of the Treasury that she has “serious concerns given the Chinese-owned business abandoned a New Hampshire facility” after a review by the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS) was triggered.
CFIUS examines certain foreign investments for national security risks.
“I’m further concerned that the Fairfield City Attorney David Lim said publicly that it’s best to fly under the radar and not get the federal government CFIUS involved,” Moy wrote.
Advertisement
The Fairfield City Council voted 6-1 on Nov. 17 to approve a 15-year water agreement supporting Streamfill’s planned operations at the former Anheuser-Busch brewery.
The agreement allows average daily use of 1.65 million gallons, rising to 2.2 million on peak days — roughly 10% of Fairfield’s daily water usage.
Vice Mayor Pam Bertani — who pressed company and city officials during last week’s council meeting to make a CFIUS filing a condition of the contract — cast the lone dissenting vote.
Advertisement

Nongfu abandoned its proposed bottling operation in Nashua, New Hampshire, following scrutiny over water demand and national security. A New Hampshire investigation found no wrongdoing by state officials but said federal review would have been advisable.
“We do need the jobs, we do need the money – but you don’t sell out your nation for that,” Moy previously told the California Post about the Fairfield deal.
Advertisement
In her letter to Garamendi, Moy questioned whether his office had been briefed on Streamfill’s full corporate structure before Fairfield approved the agreement.

She requested “a thorough national security review” examining the site’s proximity to Travis Air Force Base and what she characterized as foreign control over significant municipal water infrastructure and industrial operations along Interstate 80.
Advertisement

Garamendi’s office and the Treasury Department did not respond to the California Post’s requests for comment. Fairfield officials deferred comment to Streamfill Packers, which had not responded as of publication time.
City officials previously said Nongfu intended to pursue a voluntary review.

Filings under CFIUS’ real estate rules are voluntary. However, the committee can investigate covered transactions even if the parties do not submit a filing. Its jurisdiction can extend well beyond a mile from certain military installations.
Advertisement
Moy also flagged City Attorney David Lim’s warning that attracting the Trump administration’s attention could create political problems for Fairfield.
At the council meeting, Lim discouraged adding language requiring Streamfill to follow through on its promised filing.
“It’s kind of well known that we are not necessarily the favorite state of this current administration,” Lim said.

“I think even talking about it now, you’re probably going to draw some media attention to this, and this administration may take it out on you all, and I can’t protect you from that.”

Meanwhile, Fairfield announced on Friday that Ocean West Capital Partners had acquired the brewery property and would lease it to Streamfill. Streamfill reportedly plans to invest more than $200 million and initially create about 130 jobs.

Travis Air Force Base issued a statement to the California Post saying it takes potential national security concerns seriously but did not say whether it had sought a federal review of the Fairfield project.

“We take potential national security concerns seriously and work through established Department of War and federal channels, including processes associated with the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (CFIUS), when applicable, to ensure appropriate consideration,” officials said.
“We remain committed to safeguarding the Travis AFB mission while maintaining strong partnerships with our surrounding communities.”

articles.headline: Newsom urges reforms to presidential pardon power: ‘Justice is not for sale’
keyFacts: California Governor Gavin Newsom called for presidential pardon reforms, accusing Donald Trump of putting executive clemency up for sale.
Newsom spoke out after Trump criticized the governor's plan to commute 548 California death sentences.
Representative Jamie Raskin said he plans to investigate intermediaries who help clients obtain presidential clemency from Trump.
body: Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-CA) on Monday called for reforms of presidential pardon power, accusing President Donald Trump of putting his executive power up for sale and making the Justice Department his “law firm.”

The California governor’s comments mark the latest public skirmish with Trump after the president condemned Newsom’s plan to commute 548 California death sentences . The president held the press conference at the DOJ alongside victims’ families of the inmates who had their sentences commuted and announced a directive that would tell federal prosecutors to seek the death penalty in child murder cases and in cases involving rape or human trafficking in which the offender kills the victim.
Newsom, a possible 2028 presidential candidate, posted a video to X offering his rebuttal to Trump, laying out what he frames as instances of the president mishandling justice.
“A Justice Department is not Donald Trump’s law firm. Justice is not for sale, not in California, and not in America,” Newsom said.
He appeared to frame Trump’s press conference at the DOJ as ironic, saying, “Let’s talk about protecting families, Donald.”

Newsom cited six instances in which he claims Trump tipped the scales of justice or acted improperly, the first being the president’s actions in the 1989 Central Park Five case in which he took out newspaper ads calling for the death penalty of five young black men accused of attacking a jogger in New York City. The governor said Trump “never apologized” after the men were exonerated by DNA evidence in 2002.

“To the families standing with him today, your grief is real,” Newsom continued. “That’s why every person, every person on California’s former death row, will die in prison. No one walks out. Donald Trump’s criminals, they walk out.”

The governor went on to note pardons signed by Trump: Paul Walczak , who was pardoned of tax evasion last year after his mother, a donor to Trump, attended a dinner at the president’s Mar-a-Lago club; four private military contractors for Blackwater, who were pardoned in 2020 after they were convicted in connection with the 2007 Nisour Square massacre in Baghdad that left 14 Iraqi civilians dead; Andrew Taake, who was charged in connection to the Jan. 6, 2021, Capitol riot and pardoned by Trump upon resuming office; and the former president of Honduras, Juan Orlando Hernandez , who was pardoned in 2025 after being convicted on charges related to trafficking over 400 tons of cocaine into the United States.

“Donald Trump doesn’t oppose mercy; he sells it,” Newsom said. “If you’re poor, black or brown, you get the needle. If you’re rich and know Donald Trump, you get a pardon and a personal phone call, and he’s told you more are coming.”

Newsom additionally noted a controversy emerging involving Trump’s former personal attorney, Alina Habba. The New York Times reported that Habba secured a contract worth more than $50 million with a company controlled by the family of Venezuelan banker Julio Herrera Velutini, whom Trump pardoned in January. The agreement was reached while Habba was still working for the DOJ. Trump has publicly condemned the agreement.

“A Justice Department that prosecutes his enemies and pardons himself and his friends, that’s not law enforcement — that’s a protection racket,” Newsom said. “We need foundational federal reform, starting with this.”
“No president can ever again turn the power of mercy into a business,” he added. “No president and no one should be able to sell a pardon.”
Newsom noting the Habba controversy, as well as Trump’s pardon decisions in general, parallels that of Democrats preparing to take powerful gavels in the 120th Congress.
RASKIN SETS SIGHTS ON TRUMP ‘PARDON BROKERS’ AS DEMOCRATS PREPARE TO UNLEASH OVERSIGHT POWER

Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD), who is likely to chair the House Judiciary Committee in the Democratic majority, said he wants to investigate the emergence of the intermediaries who use their connections to Trump to help clients obtain clemency.

Raskin acknowledged that Congress has limited authority to regulate presidential pardons, as it is a power exclusive to the commander in chief. However, he suggested that the individuals facilitating those pardons could be subject to congressional scrutiny. He floated requiring individuals who lobby for pardons to register as “pardon agents” and suggested examining whether federal anti-bribery laws need to be updated to address the practice.

articles.headline: Mexico to try ‘El Chapo Isidro’ despite US extradition request
keyFacts: Mexican forces captured alleged cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores in Sinaloa following an hours-long firefight that killed 20 people.
The US requested the extradition of Meza Flores, who faces six US charges including running a continuing criminal enterprise.
Attorney General Ernestina Godoy said Mexican authorities will put Meza Flores on trial in Mexico despite the US extradition request.
body: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, an alleged cartel leader known as “El Chapo Isidro”, will be tried in Mexico despite an extradition request by the US, in a move that could worsen already-strained relations between the two countries.
Attorney General Ernestina Godoy told reporters on Monday that Mexican authorities “are going to put him on trial in this country”.

Meza Flores, one of the FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives, was captured after an hours-long firefight between Mexican forces and cartel gunmen on Friday at a compound in Guasave, in the northwestern state of Sinaloa. He was flown to Mexico City the following day.
He faces local charges for weapons offences and methamphetamine possession with intent to sell.
US involvement
Earlier on Monday, Security Minister Omar Garcia Harfuch said Washington had requested Meza Flores’s extradition after his capture in the northern state of Sinaloa.
President Claudia Sheinbaum said US authorities provided intelligence support but did not participate directly on the ground.
US surveillance drones were authorised to help track Meza Flores before the raid, authorities added, despite sensitivities over US anti-drug operations in the country in recent months.
Four Mexican soldiers and 16 alleged cartel gunmen were killed in the overnight operation, according to the Mexican Secretariat of National Defence.
Meza Flores is accused by US authorities of leading a major trafficking network that moved heroin, cocaine, methamphetamine, marijuana and fentanyl across the border.
The US Department of Justice said he faces six charges in the US that include running a continuing criminal enterprise, narcoterrorism, money laundering conspiracy and weapons offences.

His arrest is the latest in a series of high-profile anti-cartel operations by Mexico, including the February killing of Nemesio “El Mencho” Oseguera, as US President Donald ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌Trump presses ‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌‌the Sheinbaum government to crack down on organised crime.

articles.headline: Uber Riders Can Now Request to Have Their Trips Recorded
keyFacts: Uber riders in four US cities can now request video-recorded trips through a new Recorded Rides option in the app.
Uber said the feature aims to boost safety by matching riders with drivers who record encrypted video without affecting fares.
Uber said it plans to proactively activate recordings during late-night trips, teen rides, off-course routes, or detected crashes.
body: Starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a new Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber says that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”

After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.
According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.
More from CNET
While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

Starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.
Uber’s Record My Ride program
Record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.
Uber says the recordings are encrypted and stored on the driver’s device to protect the privacy of drivers and riders, and are automatically deleted after a period of time.
“Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

Not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

“Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”
Automating recordings for safety

Uber says it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

Uber says it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.

articles.headline: GTA 6's Best Easter Egg Is a Classic Tom Cruise Crime-Thriller You Can Stream For Free
keyFacts: Grand Theft Auto 6 features a random encounter where players offer a taxi ride to a character resembling Tom Cruise from the movie Collateral.
Polygon reports that players can transport this armed stranger to Harborside Park to help fight criminals and collect valuable loot.
The 2004 thriller Collateral, which inspired the game reference, is currently streaming for free on Pluto TV.
body: One of Grand Theft Auto 6’s strangest random encounters occurs when you’re offering taxi services, and a man with a beard wearing a dark suit and sunglasses climbs into the backseat with a gun. This can happen if you’re playing as either Jason or Lucia, but both scenes play out the same way: The man wants you to run a red light, ignore phone calls, and drive him to Harborside Park in Vice Beach. He also sounds an awful lot like Tom Cruise, with a calm but forceful demeanor that seems almost sociopathic. Several clips of the sequence have already hit the internet, and to many people, it’s an obvious nod to Collateral, Michael Mann’s 2004 thriller about a hitman who takes a cab driver hostage.

Jason or Lucia gets a better deal than Mann’s cabbie in this Easter egg. If you take the stranger to his destination and follow him inside after he takes out some of the criminals there, you can find a ton of valuable loot. Most players seem keen on eliminating the stranger rather than keep driving him around. In Collateral, Jamie Foxx’s character, Max, has to spend the whole night driving Cruise’s Vincent around Los Angeles. If you’ve never seen how that goes for him, Collateral is streaming for free on Pluto TV — and it’s a must-watch, especially if you want a movie that has a vibe as wild and crime-filled as GTA 6’s.

Max is a cab driver who’s been telling himself for years that the job is temporary. He wants to start his own limo company someday, so when a well-dressed passenger named Vincent (Cruise) offers him $600 to drive him around for the night, it seems like the kind of opportunity that could get him a little closer to quitting. Then a body lands on his cab at their first destination. Vincent has five people to kill before the night is over. Max has just agreed to drive him to all five stops — and he’s already an accomplice.

Vincent is one of Cruise’s best roles because so much of what makes him convincing as an action hero makes him downright scary here. The same certainty that lets Ethan Hunt talk somebody into jumping out of a plane makes it seem perfectly reasonable, for about half a second, when Vincent asks Max to help him stuff a body in the trunk. He’s also an obnoxious backseat driver. The longer he spends in the cab, the more interested he becomes in why Max has seemingly wasted so much of his life. Some of his advice is irritatingly solid, yet he’s also a man who could end the conversation with a single gunshot whenever he wanted to.

Despite the plot focusing entirely on Vincent’s assassinations, Foxx emerges as the real heart of Collateral. Early on, he picks up a prosecutor named Annie (Jada Pinkett Smith), and their conversation has the easy rhythm of two strangers who realize they’d like the ride to last a little longer. You get to see how good Max is at putting people at ease as he flirts a little. Then, Vincent hops in the back, and the nightmare begins. Once the hitman is in the car, even the smallest decisions Max makes — like when to look in the rear-view mirror and when to keep his eyes on the road — feel like consequential choices Max must make carefully.

For a movie about a man on a deadline, Collateral is remarkably willing to pull over and look around. Vincent himself comments early on about how much he despises the city’s sprawling, depersonalized atmosphere. Mann often dwells on that atmosphere to build up tension. In the movie's best quiet moment, a coyote crosses the road in front of the cab, and both men stop talking to watch it. Los Angeles feels eerie and sinister, lit by flickering streetlights and bland storefronts. As their night continues, even mundane locations feel like the most dangerous places in Los Angeles.

The story’s arc is also immensely satisfying. We see what this pressure cooker does to Max, forcing him to evolve from a passive bystander in his own life to someone who takes an active role. The evolution is subtle at first as Max resists Vincent’s demands, eventually mustering up the courage to become openly defiant. Vincent spends the night needling Max about all the chances he’s too scared to take — putting a down payment on a limo, calling Annie since she left him her card, etc. — and by the time they inevitably face off, Max is finally willing to take one.

GTA 6 so often positions your character as the Vincent of its story, stealing cars and killing people for the next big score. But forcing you to become something closer to Max, at least for a little while, is nothing short of brilliant. The Grand Theft Auto franchise at large owes a great deal of its overall vibe to Mann’s filmography. GTA 5, in particular, is largely inspired by Mann’s 1995 crime film Heat. So it's only fitting that its direct sequel pays homage to another Michael Mann classic — with a little bit of Miami Vice thrown in too, for good measure.
Collateral is available to stream for free on Pluto TV and with a subscription on Paramount Plus.

articles.headline: Power demands at AI data centers set to double by 2030 — adding the equivalent of another Great Britain to the grid as an extra $4 trillion in spending kicks in
keyFacts: The IEA reported that global data center electricity demand could double before 2030 as AI infrastructure investments accelerate.
Major artificial intelligence facilities are expanding faster than electricity networks can build transmission infrastructure to power them.
The IEA expects emissions from coal and natural gas consumed by data centers to increase by 70% before 2030.
body: - AI data center electricity demand could double before the decade ends
- More than 90 major AI facilities could require 50GW when completed
- New computing projects are advancing faster than electricity networks can expand
Artificial intelligence is driving an unprecedented expansion of computing infrastructure, forcing electricity providers to prepare for substantial increases in consumption.
The International Energy Agency (IEA) has claimed electricity requirements from data centers worldwide could double before 2030 as investment in AI infrastructure accelerates.
The additional consumption could place electricity networks under considerable pressure, particularly where existing infrastructure cannot accommodate new industrial-scale computing facilities.
AI infrastructure threatens to overwhelm existing electricity networks
According to the IEA's World Energy Outlook 2026, global data center capacity currently stands at approximately 120GW across different computing operations.
Another 120GW is expected to become operational before 2030, with artificial intelligence facilities accounting for approximately 75% of that additional capacity.
The agency has also identified 93 major AI computing facilities currently being constructed or expanded through satellite imagery and infrastructure monitoring.
Their combined electricity capacity has increased from below 2GW to approximately 17GW within just two years.

Once completed, these facilities could collectively require approximately 50GW, creating electricity demand comparable to that of Great Britain.
Meanwhile, investment in AI infrastructure should reach $32 trillion by 2050, exceeding spending associated with several major technological developments combined.
The immediate challenge involves connecting these facilities to electricity networks before their construction and expansion schedules are disrupted.
Renewable electricity projects generally require between one and five years for completion, while transmission infrastructure can take three to five times longer.
Consequently, electricity providers could struggle to deliver additional capacity quickly enough to accommodate the expanding computing industry.
Some technology companies are therefore considering independent electricity generation instead of relying entirely on conventional grid connections.
However, deploying gas turbines and other generation equipment introduces additional challenges, including equipment shortages and difficulties obtaining essential turbine components.
Rising electricity consumption raises questions about prices and emissions
The expansion has also generated opposition from communities concerned about electricity prices, particularly where large computing facilities require substantial infrastructure improvements.
The IEA says available evidence has not established a consistent connection between increasing data center capacity and higher electricity prices.
Where existing electricity infrastructure has sufficient capacity and operators cover their associated expenses, additional consumption could potentially benefit other customers.
However, circumstances could change when electricity providers must construct additional transmission lines, substations and generation facilities.
If these investments are financed through charges shared across the electricity network, households and smaller businesses could experience higher monthly bills.
Environmental considerations also complicate the industry's increasing electricity requirements, despite growing commitments to renewable energy procurement.
Renewable sources account for nearly 50% of electricity purchase agreements associated with data centers, while coal and natural gas supply approximately 60% of their actual consumption.
However, the IEA expects emissions associated with coal and natural gas consumption by data centers to increase by 70% before 2030.
“The Hormuz crisis has delivered a huge shock to the system…And I don’t see any credible pathway for the energy world to return to the way it was before,” said IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol.
“In pursuit of greater energy security, countries must take care not to replace one dependency with another.”
