articles.headline: Cisco and OpenAI pitch eBPF kernel plugins as the way to tame the patchpocalypse
keyFacts: Cisco and OpenAI released an open-source tool called Shirudo that uses eBPF to protect Linux systems without needing immediate patches.
The companies said Shirudo helps organizations cope with over 100,000 software flaws reported this year.
The system uses AI to generate security shields, which the companies envision humans checking before production deployment.
body: Cisco and OpenAI have released an open-source tool called Shirudo to implement compensating controls in Linux, potentially improving security for users who can’t quickly patch newly discovered software flaws.

Shirudo relies on eBPF, the technology that makes it possible to run sandboxed programs in the Linux kernel. eBPF programs are effectively kernel plug-ins but don’t get unrestricted access to system resources.
Developers have mostly used eBPF to create network functions that enable things like the open source Kubernetes observability and security tool Cilium , a Cloud Native Computing Foundation project.
Cisco and OpenAI think eBPF can help organizations cope with the flood of 100,000-plus software flaws reported this year, many after the debut of AI-powered bug finders.

The increased volume of flaws, and patches to fix them, is a problem for many organizations which already struggle to test fixes or find change windows in which to implement them. That problem has seen greater interest in “compensating controls” – changes to applications or infrastructure that harden them against flaws or malware, without requiring a patch.
With Shirudo, Cisco and OpenAI are suggesting two things:
The privileges eBPF programs enjoy make them a fine way to implement compensating controls for Linux;
Agents should scan your infrastructure for vulnerabilities, then use tools like OpenAI’s Codex to write compensating controls as eBPF programs at machine speed.

“Shirudo” is apparently the Japanese word for “shield,” so Cisco and OpenAI have called the eBPF programs the tool creates “shields.” The two companies envision humans checking every shield Shirudo creates before putting it into production.

Shirudo is open source and available here . The two companies say they’ve already demonstrated it could mitigate the recently discovered flaws in Java without requiring downtime for an Elasticsearch implementation.

Cisco and OpenAI are not alone in advocating for compensating controls. Third-party software maintenance outfits like Rimini Street have used them for years to protect software when their clients no longer have the right to access patches. VMware has introduced “virtual patching.” Palo Alto Networks and Rapid 7 also like this approach, and offer automation to develop controls.
Where Cisco and OpenAI differ is their decision to make Shirudo open source , and their ambition that other players adapt and advance it.

That offer is not entirely altruistic, as if Shirudo takes off it could create more demand for Codex. Cisco’s angle comes from the fact it owns Isovalent, an early champion of eBPF and the creator of both Cilium and the Tetragon sub-project on which Shirudo is based. Switchzilla is using eBPF in other products, so normalizing its use through an open source project can’t hurt. ®

articles.headline: The three DISM commands you should know to fix your Windows system images
keyFacts: Windows includes a built-in Deployment Image Servicing and Management utility to scan and repair corrupt system files.
The utility uses CheckHealth, ScanHealth, and RestoreHealth commands executed with administrator privileges in Command Prompt or PowerShell.
If Windows Update fails, users can repair files using Windows installation media and then run the System File Checker command.
body: The three DISM commands you should know to fix your Windows system images
Check and repair damaged system files with these DISM commands.

Your Windows installation depends on a collection of important system files to run applications, install updates and perform everyday computing tasks. If these files get damaged or go missing, your system may behave erratically. You may encounter system errors, features not working as expected, freezes or other unexpected behavior. Sometimes restarting your computer or running the usual troubleshooting steps aren't enough to restore damaged system files. For such cases, Windows provides a built-in repair utility called Deployment Image Servicing and Management (DISM).

DISM is a command line tool that can scan Windows system images for corrupt system files and attempt repairs. Particularly, there are three useful DISM commands that achieve this purpose: CheckHealth, ScanHealth and RestoreHealth. You can run DISM commands in either the command prompt or the PowerShell, but both CLIs require administrator privileges to make system-level changes. It's worth noting that DISM exclusively scans and repairs system files; your personal files remain untouched.
Three DISM commands that fix damaged Windows installation

All three DISM commands in question follow a specific syntax that begins with DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image. The parts following "DISM" in the syntax are called command-line options. The /Online CLI option specifies DISM to take action on the currently running Windows installation, while /Cleanup-Image performs recovery operations on the selected installation.

The first command is DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth. It checks whether Windows has already flagged corrupt system files and whether the corruption is repairable. This is the first recommended step when investigating corrupt system files as it takes very little time to complete.

The next command is DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth and it works slightly differently from the CheckHealth command. Unlike CheckHealth, the ScanHealth DISM command performs a fresh scan of your system files and reports any its findings. The ScanHealth operation may take several minutes to complete, but it provides you with a fresh report on the component store's health.

Finally, the DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth command both scans the component store for corruption and attempts to repair them automatically. By default, RestoreHealth uses Windows Update to obtain the necessary system files needed to repair the component store. The Windows component store is a protected internal repository that contains important system files. Windows requires these files to service, update and customize the operating system.
What to do if DISM fails to repair your Windows installation?

Sometimes system file damage can also break Windows Update, preventing DISM from downloading replacement files. When this happens, you can use an official Windows installation media to supply DISM with the necessary repair files. You can download a Windows ISO from Microsoft's official download page. Once downloaded, right click the ISO file and select mount. Windows will create a virtual drive for the ISO, assign it a drive letter and make its contents available.

Next, you'll need to check the Windows editions available in the downloaded installation media. You can do that by launching the command prompt as an administrator and running the DISM /Get-ImageInfo /ImageFile:D:sourcesinstall.wim command. This command lists the Windows editions available on the installation media along with their index numbers. Make a note of the index number corresponding to your installed edition before proceeding to the next step.

Now, run the DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth /Source:WIM:D:sourcesinstall.wim:6 /LimitAccess command. Replace D: with the drive letter assigned to the mounted Windows ISO and 6 with the index number corresponding to your Windows edition. This directs DISM to use the installation media as its repair source instead of downloading files from Windows Update.

Once DISM completes its operation, run the sfc /scannow command to repair damaged or missing system files. Microsoft recommends running the DISM repair utility before System File Checker (SFC) because DISM repairs the Windows component store, which SFC relies on to replace corrupted system files.

articles.headline: Trump claims credit for Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia, posts meme depicting Huang holding up a bra victoriously
keyFacts: US President Donald Trump stated that he personally convinced the Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.
The Nvidia board voted unanimously to bring Huang back after receiving input from senior levels of the United States government.
Lawmakers from both parties raised national security and corruption concerns, and Huang is set to testify before the US Senate on December 3.
body: US President Donald Trump told CNBC on Monday that he personally "convinced" the Nvidia board to reinstate Jensen Huang.

Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO a little under two weeks ago after admitting to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang (no relation), who formerly controlled Singaporean tech company Megaspeed International and has been the subject of US national security concerns related to AI chip exports to China.

Following the admission, as well as reports of two other affairs with Nvidia employees, Huang resigned as Nvidia president, CEO, and board member. Last week, amid calls for Huang's return from tech CEOs and investors, the Nvidia board said firmly that it would not reinstate him.

Cue the It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia title card: The gang reinstated him. On Monday, the Nvidia board said that it had "voted unanimously" to bring Huang back after receiving "input from senior levels of the United States government." Nvidia shares shot up 31.48% during Monday's trading.

Trump has taken credit for the change of heart. "I made the deal," he told CNBC. The President also posted a congratulatory AI-generated image depicting Huang as himself surviving an attempted assassination while holding up a red bra victoriously.
The news of Huang's reinstatement prompted a flurry of responses from US congressmembers on Monday.

"President Trump's direct involvement with Nvidia’s decision to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang raises serious national security and corruption questions. We must investigate these actions," said California Democratic congressman Robert Garcia in a statement. "No president who has invested in a private company should be involved in their board decisions. Congress must come together in swift bipartisan action and demand answers immediately."
Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.
It hasn't just been Democrats criticizing Huang's reinstatement.

"Jensen Huang had multiple affairs including with subordinates and an alleged Chinese spy. His own board described his behavior as lacking 'candor,'" said Republican senator Pete Ricketts of Nebraska. "I've served on a public company board. His behavior does not support reinstatement."

"The risk of extortion by a Chinese asset who's been banned by Singapore is risk enough to not rehire Huang," said North Dakota Republican Kevin Cramer. "The worst part of this is what we may never know. Congress should immediately pass the strictest export controls possible. I hope it’s not too late."
Huang is set to testify before the US Senate next Thursday, December 3.

articles.headline: Unsealed warrant documents for Ilhan Omar's DC home raid reveal decades-long scope of investigation
keyFacts: Redacted warrant documents released Monday reveal federal prosecutors are investigating Rep. Ilhan Omar for alleged crimes spanning from 1980 to present.
Investigators raided Omar's Washington residence in October 2026 as part of a probe into potential immigration paperwork fraud, sources said.
Omar has not been charged with any crime and her office characterized the federal investigation as politically motivated by Donald Trump.
body: Heavily redacted versions of documents used to justify a search warrant and raid on the Washington, D.C. home of Rep. Ilhan Omar , D-Minn., were released to the public Monday evening.
Despite the level of redaction, the documents provide more insight into the scope of the investigation into the Somali-born congresswoman.

In an ex parte brief in support of an affidavit for a search warrant, federal prosecutors say they're searching for all "records and information that constitute fruits, contraband, evidence, and instrumentalities of violations of [redacted], those violations involving Ilhan Nur Said Elmi a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar, and occurring between 1980 to the present (the 'Target Offenses)."

While accounts vary, even from the congresswoman herself, Omar was born in 1981 or 1982. She does not have a birth certificate. She came to the United States in 1995 with her father. Fox News Digital confirmed just after the Oct. 12 raid of her home, that investigators were looking into alleged immigration fraud, potentially related to how Omar and her father filled out her immigration paperwork.
In another document, arguing that the court mischaracterized the government's arguments in ex parte proceedings, prosecutors make it clear that the investigation into Omar spans decades.
"The United States believes that ILHAN has committed [REDACTED] crimes over decades— beginning long before she was ever in Congress," the document says.
Fox News Digital reached out to a spokesperson for Omar.

In a rare move, Obama-appointed federal Judge James Boasberg ordered the documents' release last week, telling the Department of Justice (DOJ) to submit proposed redactions before the materials were made public on Monday. Judge Boasberg, in order dated October 9, 2026, agreed initially to seal the documents due to "such reasonable grounds to believe the disclosure will result in flight from prosecution, destruction of or tampering with evidence, intimidation of potential witnesses, and serious jeopardy to the investigation."
Search warrants typically remain sealed until there is an arrest in a criminal case.

Fifteen media outlets, led by The New York Times , along with watchdog group Judicial Watch, sued President Donald Trump's DOJ for the release of the documents used to conduct the raid of a sitting congresswoman's residence. The outlets claimed that viewing the documents was in the public interest, while the government attempted to block the release by arguing that it was a violation of investigative protocol.
OBAMA-APPOINTED JUDGE PAVES WAY TO UNSEAL ILHAN OMAR SEARCH WARRANT IN BLOW TO TRUMP'S DOJ

Omar's Washington, D.C., home was raided on Oct. 12, 2026 — an unprecedented action to take against a sitting lawmaker, especially when there is less than a month until the Election Day where they are seeking reelection. The raid did not impact Omar in winning a fifth term in the House of Representatives.

Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), the chief investigative body of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), conducted the raid last month. Omar's personal phone, computer and passport were seized as evidence in the search. Authorities are also in possession of her DNA.

Additionally, the lawmaker's sister, Sahra Noor , voluntarily submitted to questions from investigators during the week of the raid. Investigators are probing whether Omar or her late father — or both — lied on her citizenship paperwork, sources told Fox News Digital.

In a motion seeking to prevent the federal search warrant for the raid from being unsealed, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia referred to Omar as "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar." Sources later told Fox News Digital that Ilhan Omar is not the congresswoman's "real name."
REP ILHAN OMAR'S IMMIGRATION HISTORY FACES NEW SCRUTINY AS FEDERAL INVESTIGATORS SUBPOENA RELATIVES
That news caused speculation that Omar married her brother, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi , to resurface. The pair married in 2009, and divorced in 2017.
Omar has not been charged with a crime and has repeatedly denied wrongdoing. She has characterized the investigation as politically motivated, saying President Donald Trump is targeting her.

"For a decade, Donald Trump has relentlessly targeted Congresswoman Ilhan Omar with inflammatory rhetoric, repeatedly putting a target on her back," her office said in a statement after the raid. "Now, those attacks have escalated to a pointless federal raid. The Congresswoman has done nothing wrong. No president should be able to use the power of the federal government to intimidate his political enemies."

The Somali-born congresswoman came to the United States as a child in 1995, after decades of civil unrest in her home country. Her father, Nur Omar Mohamed, served as a colonel in the Somali National Army under the brutal Siad Barre regime.
Barre's regime systematically killed between 50,000 and 200,000 members of the Isaaq clan in what is known as the Isaaq genocide. He was deposed in 1991.

articles.headline: Google alternative Kagi launches an email service
keyFacts: Kagi announced the public beta launch of Kagi Mail, a new email service competing with Gmail.
The service includes 50GB of storage and costs $99 per year after a 60-day free trial.
Kagi plans to add an address book in early 2027 and native mobile apps in late 2027.
body: Kagi, which already offers a paid alternative to Google Search and its own Orion browser as a rival to Chrome, is taking on another Google service: Gmail. Today, Kagi announced a public beta of Kagi Mail, a new email service that has “no surveillance, no ads, open standards, and no lock-in.”
Google alternative Kagi launches an email service
Kagi Mail is launching in public beta with a 60-day free trial.

With Kagi Mail, you get an @kagimail.com address, but the service also supports unlimited aliases and domains. It also offers 50GB of storage and a built-in calendar. On the roadmap, you can expect contacts and an address book in Q1 2027, but native mobile apps aren’t expected to arrive until Q3 2027.

“Does the world need another email service? We asked ourselves that question more than once,” Kagi says. “There are great ones out there, and we’re fans of what Fastmail and Tuta are doing. We still built our own, for the same reason we build everything at Kagi: technology should do its job and then get out of your way.”
Kagi Mail is available now with a 60-day free trial before you have to pay $99 per year. The service is available as part of a $25 per month Kagi Ultimate subscription.

articles.headline: Can You Romance Vicki In GTA 6?
keyFacts: Players meet the side character Vicki during Chapter 2 of Grand Theft Auto 6 while playing as Lucia.
According to the article, it is not possible to romance Vicki at any point in the game for either Jason or Lucia.
Players can see a brief secret dance by Vicki at Delights Cabaret during a specific mission and can still contact her by phone later.
body: The main story in Grand Theft Auto 6 actively pushes Jason and Lucia into a romantic relationship, even though the player can resist it, if they prefer. However, there are plenty of other side characters that players would like the chance to try to romance, and one character near the top of that list is Vicki.

Similar to Mandy, another potential romance partner in GTA 6 , many find Vicki to be an attractive side character who plays a role in the main story. Narratively speaking, Vicki is more of a factor than Mandy, but she shows less romantic interest in either Jason or Lucia. Still, in a game where anything is possible, you might be wondering whether it's possible to romance Vicki in GTA 6.
Is Vicki romanceable in GTA 6?

Initially, you meet Vicki when playing as Lucia near the start of Chapter 2, which takes place in Kelly County. At this point in the story, Lucia is getting most of the screen time while Jason is unplayable for story reasons we won't spoil.
The pair are holed up in the Starlet Motel for the time being and in need of medication. Lucia finds out that a woman named Vicki at the Starlet Motel apparently sells drugs that can do the trick.

From here, Lucia and Vicki get into all sorts of hijinks together, along with the help of a degenerate named Dunk. You'll eventually finish Vicki's story after a robbery at Delights Cabaret, which is the strip club where Vicki works.

Unfortunately, throughout all of these interactions, it's not possible to romance Vicki at any point in GTA 6 . This goes for both Jason and Lucia, as Vicki is seemingly only interested in doing business, not business time .

However, there is a brief interaction you can have with Vicki if you act quickly. Prior to the end of the "Painkiller" mission in GTA 6, which sees Lucia running around trying to get the meds, you can catch a special dance from Vicki at Delights Cabaret. Vicki goes on stage and does a dance, with her clothes on, for the audience at the club. During this point, you'll still be playing as Lucia, so she'll be the one at the club if you see Vicki's dance.

This isn't a romance option for Vicki, as she will dance whether you're there or not, but it is a secret encounter that lets you see more of her character in GTA 6. After the Painkiller mission ends, though, you won't be able to see her dance at Delights again.

If you happened to miss out on Vicki's dance, you can technically see more of her by visiting Snapmatic on your phone. You're also free to call or text Vicki, as she will respond even after chapter 2 ends in GTA 6.

articles.headline: Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?
keyFacts: BBC football pundit Troy Deeney selected his Premier League team and manager of the week following the latest round of matches.

Selected players included Konstantinos Tzolakis, James Hill, Malick Thiaw, Keane Lewis-Potter, Noah Okafor, Jack Rudoni, Elliott Anderson, Luca Williams-Barnett, Florian Wirtz, Oli McBurnie, and Rio Ngumoha.
Frank Lampard was chosen as the manager of the week after securing a win for Coventry.
body: - Published
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.
Here are this week's choices. Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

Konstantinos Tzolakis (Hull City): If you watched the Brighton game and wondered how on earth Hull won it was because Konstantinos Tzolakis was in goal. An unbelievable performance with five or six top-class saves. Big moments, big personality, he has stepped up every time. He's been one of the players of the season - I know it's a bit too early to crown people but if it stopped now he has to be goalkeeper of the season.

James Hill (Bournemouth): He backed up getting into the England squad. Sometimes when people get called up they start to get above their stations but he didn't do that at all. He was in a really good state of form. A cheeky assist as well but defensively solid. He has been in my team a few times now - a centre-half who does his job without complaining.
Malick Thiaw (Newcastle): He divides opinion but he played really well and got his goal.
Keane Lewis-Potter (Brentford): Two goals against Everton and that was before the sending-off of James Tarkowski. Performed well again. Sneaky bargain buy of the century to be honest.

Noah Okafor (Leeds): Two goals again. Leeds battered Chelsea and made them look unbelievably average. Nobody has been talking about how sneaky good Leeds have been, some really big performances this season.
Jack Rudoni (Coventry): Two assists in a must-win game against Crystal Palace. He stepped up big, fair play to him.

Elliott Anderson (Manchester City): The only person who actually showed a pulse in this game. He got a goal and showed pace and showed he wanted to be there. He tried his best to win a game of football.

Luca Williams-Barnett (Tottenham): Young man, a with goal and an assist. He just gave Spurs a spark we haven't seen for probably six or seven years now. He gave them that spark instantly and fair play to De Zerbi for putting him in. All the money spent, who knew it would be a home-grown talent in their youth team who would step up and really get the Spurs fans excited.

Florian Wirtz (Liverpool): Unbelievable performance. He has had a bit of a purple patch since Jurgen Klopp has taken over Germany. Did really well in terms of finding the gaps, drifting between players and finding through balls and now adding goals. Now we are seeing the player we saw in Germany and I am buzzing for him.

Oli McBurnie (Hull City): The man of the moment. He works really hard, he does everything for the team to make sure they are there. He is solid defensively but then he gets two shots and two goals. Top performance from him.

Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool): He made Diogo Dalot look like he'd never played a game before, not the fact he has played over 250 games for Manchester United and has gone to World Cups with Portugal and made him look childish, Ran him every time and twisted him inside out and got his goal.

Frank Lampard (Coventry): In the biggest game of the season so far for him he made sure he got the job done. Big win. No new-manager bounce for Palace as Lampard gets the job done and he made some big calls.

articles.headline: Mark Allen sends heartfelt message to fans after brave mental health battle
keyFacts: Snooker player Mark Allen thanked supporters on social media while admitting he is currently in a major low amid mental health struggles.
Allen previously spent ten weeks in a mental health clinic and recently returned to competition after a five-month absence.
Allen cast doubt over his participation in the upcoming UK Championship as he continues working on his recovery.
body: Mark Allen has admitted he is ‘in a major low’ as he thanked supporters for their support amid his mental health struggles .
The snooker star bravely opened up on his recent battle in October, where he revealed he had been in a mental health clinic for months before being discharged to play in the Northern Ireland Open.
Allen’s recent woes began when he suffered a World Championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in April Getty
Allen was beaten by Jordan Brown in the opening round in Belfast last month after five months away from snooke r.
He gave an emotional interview with TNT Sports afterwards, where he admitted he was in a ‘bad place’ and and was considering retiring.
Following his losing return, Allen said live on air: “I’ve been flooded with support, but problems are within.
“I just don’t see a future of us sticking in it, if I’m honest.

“It’s sad to say because it’s all I’ve loved to do since I was 12, but the last few months have been really difficult, and it sort of put snooker into perspective for me. But tonight, I’m just trying to survive.”
A day later, the former world No.1 then released a statement and disclosed that he had spent ten weeks in a mental health clinic and discharged himself to prepare for his return to snooker.
Allen update on ‘very tough’ period
Almost a month after his heartbreaking update, Allen took to social media to thank fans for their support as he admitted he has endured a difficult past few weeks .
He wrote on X: “Haven’t been on in a while but inundated with messages…….
“The last few weeks have been very tough for me. I continue to work hard on my recovery but definitely stuck in a major low right now. Not sure what’s ahead really.
“Thanks everyone for the messages though, they don’t go unnoticed.”
View Tweet: https://t.co/9v6wvWMflE
Allen is the only player to have made maximum breaks in all three Triple Crown tournaments, Getty
Allen appeared to cast renewed doubt over his future in snooker in his latest post, and his involvement in this week’s UK Championship .
Currently ranked No.12 in the world, the Northern Irishman is listed among the top 16 seeds for the first of the Triple Crown events in York, making him an automatic qualifier for the main round.
However, he is yet to confirm whether or not he will be competing in the major which gets underway this Saturday, just weeks after sharing fresh hope that he could feature.
Thanking fans in a previous post in October, he had said: “Completely overwhelmed by all the messages I have received since my statement.
“As I continue my treatment and my recovery [I] now know that I simply have to raise more awareness around mental health in the future.
“Best part of six weeks before the UK Championships starts and all being well I’ll be in a better place by then but for now it’s just one day at a time.
Allen is one of the best players on the tour, but has barely featured in recent months Getty
“Thanks again for all your support. It’s meant so so much to myself and my family.”
Allen’s career
Since turning professional in 2005, Allen has established himself as one of the UK’s leading snooker players.
The Pistol is ranked at world No.12 after a six-month hiatus earlier this year, has won 12 ranking tournaments in his career, including the 2022 UK Championship and two Northern Ireland Open titles.
He has reached the World Championship semi-finals three times, and won the 2018 Masters – his other Triple Crown title.

articles.headline: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
keyFacts: The US Department of Commerce announced it intends to blacklist Singaporean AI company Megaspeed over suspected violations of export controls.
US officials raised concerns that Megaspeed funneled advanced Nvidia computer chips to China, aided by a former executive accused of spying.
The commerce department did not specify when the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect.
body: - Published
The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America.
The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US.

The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang.
The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China.

When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed.
Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang.
Alice Huang (no relation) was thought by US intelligence to be working as an asset for Beijing, creating national security concerns within the US.
China has denied that she is a spy and warned the US not to use the scandal as a "pretext for imposing a technological blockade" on AI technology.
On 12 November, Jensen Huang resigned after allegations he had had another affair, this one with a Nvidia employee.
On Monday, Nvidia's board reinstated him after US President Donald Trump said he had "convinced" the company and "made the deal".
The commerce department has said it had been investigating Megaspeed for almost two years.
The department said it had suspected the company was violating US export controls by helping to get Nvidia's chips into the hands of companies within China.
China has been blocked from buying such technology since 2022.
Although based in Singapore, Megaspeed has significant business dealings in China.
Alibaba, for instance, the major Chinese online retailer, has been reported to be one if its largest customers.
Megaspeed was a known buyer of billions of dollars of Nvidia computer chips, including through its subsidiary Speedmatrix, which has also been added to the Commerce blacklist.
Nvidia's computer chips, originally designed for use in gaming consols, in recent years have become crucial to the continued growth of the AI industry.

Without enough supply or access to computer chips that are capable of processing the huge amount of data needed to make things like AI chatbots and models run, AI companies will not be able to meet or grow demand from people using AI tools.
That has driven up the value of Nvidia on the stock market, as well as its influence in the AI industry and the White House.
Although tech stocks have in recent months been volatile and trending lower, when Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia because of his affairs, the company's stock fell by more than 30%.
Anxiety about the company's influence and ability to operate within the AI ecosystem without its famed executive appeared to take down shares of other tech companies, too.
Huang was reinstated on Monday to his position as head of Nvidia, a move that US President Donald Trump said he told the company's board to take.
The company's stock rallied on his reinstatement, as did several other tech stocks, but shares of Nvidia did not climb to where the company had been before being immersed in scandal.
In the weeks ahead, Huang and the company he now runs again are facing multiple government agency investigations.
Huang and the chief legal officer of Nvidia are set to appear next for a closed-door briefing with the House Foreign Affairs Committee.

articles.headline: Russian incursions into NATO territory are increasing
keyFacts: Three Russian cruise missiles struck southeastern Poland on Friday without causing casualties, Polish authorities said.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte called for continued support for Ukraine while Polish authorities investigate whether the incursions were intentional.
European leaders will discuss boosting defense on NATO's eastern flank at an EU summit later this week, German Chancellor Merz said.
body: Russian incursions into NATO territory are increasing
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte is seeking to reassure the alliance's eastern European members after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland on Friday.
SCOTT DETROW, HOST:

Russian incursions into NATO territory are increasing. NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte is seeking to reassure the alliance's Eastern European members after three Russian cruise missiles landed in Poland on Friday. While no one was hurt, Rutte was in Germany today, where he addressed growing concerns. And for more, we are joined now by Esme Nicholson in Berlin. Hey, Esme.
ESME NICHOLSON, BYLINE: Hey, Scott.

DETROW: The cruise missiles hit Poland during one of Russia's biggest aerial attacks on Ukraine since the start of the full-scale invasion. Ukraine then hit back over the weekend. So first, bring us up to speed on that.

NICHOLSON: Well, as you say, the risks of the war in Ukraine spilling over were loud and clear over the weekend. It started on Friday morning with what Polish authorities have now identified as three Russian cruise missiles striking a rural part of southeastern Poland, about 30 miles from the Ukrainian border. Now, as you say, there were no casualties, but the incursions happened while European forces were staging a military exercise in the region. And Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk calls the incident an "intentional provocation" - that's a quote.

Then on Saturday, a sanctioned Russian cargo ship in the Baltic Sea was hit by what is suspected to have been a Ukrainian maritime drone. And on Sunday, Ukraine took credit for sinking a Russian warship docked in the Libyan port of Benghazi, thousands of miles from the front line. Libyan authorities have condemned the attack in their port, reflecting broader concerns that the conflict could spread far beyond Europe.
DETROW: Right. And that is a broad battlefield that you're talking about right there. NATO's chief was in Berlin today. Does he view this as the beginning of an escalation beyond Ukraine's borders?

NICHOLSON: Well, Rutte was rather cautious in his assessment of the weekend. He was in Berlin for an annual meeting, talking to parliamentarians from NATO countries. And while he acknowledged the danger of cruise missile incursions, he was eager that Polish authorities finish their investigations to establish whether they were intentional or not. Speaking to journalists, he said the alliance has, quote, "many response options" (ph) but that he can't always be open about them. But he also appealed for public support for Ukraine.
(SOUNDBITE OF PRESS CONFERENCE)
MARK RUTTE: As societies, we have to be resilient and, most importantly, keep that support for Ukraine going. So for every incident in Europe, more support for Ukraine, not less support for Ukraine.
NICHOLSON: And Zelenskyy, who dialed into the meeting in Berlin today, urged for fresh negotiations with Russia, this time involving the Europeans.
DETROW: Let's talk more about the Europeans. What do you think the odds are that they'll end up playing a role in bringing about the end of this war?

NICHOLSON: Well, since last week's coalition of the willing meeting here in Berlin, it's looking a little more likely. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and European leaders warned the U.S. and Russia against going over their heads. And today, Merz stressed that Europe is ready to sit at the table, something U.S. special envoy for peace missions Jared Kushner supports. But Merz also made it clear that no NATO member, quote, "has any interest in an escalation in the Baltic Sea region," which some see as an appeal to Ukraine to do its part to prevent the conflict from spreading.

He vowed that European leaders would discuss boosting defense on NATO's eastern flank at an EU summit later this week. And he was also quite candid in stating that NATO made a mistake back in 2008 when it decided not to make Ukraine a member, saying that if Ukraine had been a NATO member, this war would probably have been preventable.
DETROW: That is Esme Nicholson in Berlin. Thank you so much.
NICHOLSON: Thank you, Scott.

articles.headline: Figma employee sues, alleging company forced her to confront harassers
keyFacts: Figma engineer Serry Park sued Figma and CEO Dylan Field, alleging sexual harassment, racial and gender discrimination, and retaliation.
The lawsuit claims that Figma managers and HR repeatedly instructed Park to confront her alleged harassers directly instead of investigating.
Park is seeking damages, a jury trial, and a court order prohibiting Figma from requiring employees to confront alleged harassers.
body: A Figma engineer is suing the design software company and its co-founder and CEO, Dylan Field, over allegations that she faced sexual harassment and retaliation while managers and HR repeatedly told her to confront the very people she accused of misconduct.

The lawsuit, filed Monday in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York, alleges that Figma’s culture of “direct feedback” led managers and HR to make engineer Serry Park address harassment herself rather than investigate her complaints. Park, who joined Figma in 2022, alleges the company’s response damaged her career, compensation, and mental health. The lawsuit also alleges that Park, who is Asian, faced racial and gender discrimination, including performance criticism based on stereotypes that Asian women are meek, timid, and conflict-averse.

“Figma was my dream company for a long time,” Park told TechCrunch in an interview before the lawsuit was filed. “It was a place where I felt that I could level up in my career, working on a lot of really cool, interesting things at scale.”

Park is seeking damages, a jury trial, and a court order prohibiting Figma from requiring employees who report harassment to confront their alleged harassers. She also wants the company to adopt and enforce a process for investigating harassment complaints promptly and confidentially.

When reached for comment, a spokesperson for Figma said, “Figma does not tolerate discrimination or harassment. Figma also does not tolerate extortion. These claims have no merit, and we will present the facts in court.”
Faith in the Process

Park told TechCrunch she initially had faith in Figma’s complaint process, expecting that if she documented the alleged harassment and reported it to the right people, the company would act. But as an engineer in a male-dominated field, Park told TechCrunch, “I don’t feel that they took me seriously throughout this process.”

Park, who is still employed at Figma, joined its San Francisco office in October 2022. Within weeks, her onboarding mentor — a fellow engineer — asked her on a date and continued pursuing her after she declined, Park alleges. She initially feared reporting him, worrying that her manager would “dismiss her reports or view her as the problem,” according to the lawsuit.

Park says she tried to avoid her onboarding mentor. In early 2023, for example, she delayed choosing a work project until he had picked one. When her manager criticized her for not being a “team player,” Park explained that she was trying to avoid the colleague she accused of harassment, according to the suit.

Her manager allegedly dismissed her concerns, saying he had “met his wife at work too” and treating the behavior as “harmless flirtation.” When Park asked to be kept off projects with the onboarding mentor, HR allegedly instructed her to confront him directly about his behavior.

The lawsuit ties that response to Figma’s culture of direct feedback, which Park alleges Field established and enforced. It says the company’s People organization trains managers to direct employees, including those reporting harassment, to give feedback directly to the person involved.

In March 2023, her manager assigned him to a major project she was leading, despite her request to be separated from him. Park told her manager that she would “figure it out,” but alleges that having to work with him affected her performance. Her manager gave her a 2 out of 5 on her performance review, criticizing her for not speaking up enough or engaging with others and for lacking presence. Park was put on a coaching plan, which she completed in late 2023.

Changing managers didn’t help, according to the lawsuit. Her second manager also refused to separate them, allegedly telling Park that someone at her level should be able to resolve conflicts with teammates and that separating them would be “avoiding the problem.” Like her previous manager, he allegedly pointed out that he had met his partner at work.
Park alleges the harassment continued throughout 2023.
In April 2024, she transferred to another team, a move she claims set back her career by resetting her performance and promotion timeline.

On her new team, which had more women, Park said she felt better and no longer had to work with her alleged harasser. Her performance reviews improved, but in late 2025, she alleges another incident of sexual harassment, this time by her new manager.

The incident followed a night out for drinks with her wife and two teammates, including her manager. The next day, during a team lunch, the manager allegedly said Park’s sex life had been discussed the previous evening. Park, who said no such conversation had occurred in her or her wife’s presence, felt “horrified and humiliated” by comments she believed fetishized queer relationships.

A colleague reported the comments to HR as sexual harassment, according to the suit. Weeks later, Park’s manager apologized in a Slack message, saying she didn’t recall what she had said. When Park sought HR’s guidance, she was again told to address the matter directly with her manager.

During their conversation, the manager allegedly became defensive, and the encounter left Park feeling “crushed, anxious, and vulnerable.” The manager also allegedly said she would never make such a comment because she had “a lot of gay friends.”
The manager told HR that they had agreed it was a misunderstanding. HR closed its investigation without interviewing witnesses, according to the suit, even though Park disputed her manager’s account.
“Requiring an employee to confront her harasser as the price of complaining — and then closing her complaint — would dissuade a reasonable employee from complaining at all,” the suit said.

Park alleges her manager retaliated by publicly berating her, sometimes so aggressively that colleagues intervened or checked on her afterward, according to the lawsuit. The suit also alleges that other teammates left the team over concerns about the manager’s behavior.

Park again complained to HR about “escalating retaliation” and expressed concern the manager would “derail her career.” HR allegedly defended the manager’s conduct, saying the manager was “within her reasonable authority” and again instructed Park to address her concerns directly with the manager.

In early 2026, Park received another low performance review and a reduced bonus. The lawsuit alleges that similarly situated men continued to receive promotions, raises, and bonuses. When Park reported the negative performance review to HR in March, she was allegedly told her sexual harassment complaint against her manager could not be “substantiated.”

Park took medical leave in March to receive treatment for PTSD symptoms and generalized anxiety. Cleared to return to work in June, she was prescribed workplace accommodations, including a graduated work schedule and mandatory remote workdays.

Park told TechCrunch that Figma approved the accommodations but had not implemented them at the time she returned to work. In July, Park and her lawyers notified Figma of their intent to pursue legal action.

“It’s really scary for me,” she said about taking legal action. “I don’t know what’s going to happen next with this, I don’t know what the outcome is going to be, but at least it feels like this is my chance to do the right thing.”
This piece was updated to clarify when Park said Figma implemented the recommendations from her medical professionals.

articles.headline: Why Trump saved Jensen Huang
keyFacts: Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia CEO on Monday after Donald Trump personally intervened during a weekend board meeting.
Huang's return boosted stock markets, as Nvidia's chipmaking and financing are critical to the AI industry.
Huang is set to testify in the Senate next Thursday as congressional oversight begins under incoming Democratic majorities.
body: Donald Trump greets Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang outside the West Wing of the White House on September 29, 2026. | Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images
This story appeared in The Logoff , a daily newsletter that helps you stay informed about the Trump administration without letting political news take over your life. Subscribe here .
Welcome to The Logoff: Donald Trump is personally intervening to keep the AI industry afloat.

What happened? Jensen Huang, the recently ousted Nvidia CEO, is back atop the company as of Monday morning, after Trump dialed into an Nvidia board meeting over the weekend to offer “assurance” about legal and national security concerns around Huang.

Huang’s restoration — after he resigned following reports about multiple alleged affairs, including one with a possible Chinese spy — is a remarkable reversal of fortune. It also marks an unprecedented, at least in the modern era, level of direct White House interference with corporate America.
What’s the context? This is the outcome that Trump, Elon Musk, and many of his other allies on the tech right have been agitating for since Huang stepped down not even two weeks ago.

As head of Nvidia, Huang has become — apparently quite literally — the AI industry’s “indispensable man.” In addition to being the leading maker of advanced AI chips, Nvidia is sometimes referred to as the “central bank of AI” for the financing schemes it uses to keep major labs afloat. That gives it a great deal of sway over better-known companies like OpenAI and Anthropic.
Huang, by some in the industry and on Wall Street, was considered central to those efforts. Markets jumped dramatically Monday morning on news of his return.

Why does this matter? His return is a boon for the stock market and the AI industry just as both were starting to stumble, and one that may temporarily fend off the “perfect storm” that my colleague Eric Levitz described last week .

It’s also an exceptional moment of naked self-interest by Trump, choosing the market’s continued well-being and his personal friendship with Huang over real national security concerns about Huang’s leadership at Nvidia.

What now? The Huang scandal won’t end here. He’s set to testify in the Senate next Thursday, and that’s likely just the start of the congressional oversight he can expect with incoming Democratic majorities in both chambers. After today, where that will lead is anyone’s guess.
And with that, it’s time to log off…

articles.headline: Trump halts Iowa detonation, says new governor to blame if it blows accidentally
keyFacts: President Trump ordered the US military to halt plans to detonate deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Iowa ammunition plant.
Environmental groups filed a legal challenge and a federal appeals court granted a hold on the Environmental Protection Agency permit.
The Army delayed the blast after residents and officials expressed concern over toxic gases and neurotoxic lead reaching up to 100 miles away.
body: President Trump took to social media Monday afternoon to announce that he has ordered the US military to halt plans to detonate 68 deteriorating barrels of lead azide at an Army ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa. Trump claimed that the fate of the unstable, highly explosive material is now in the hands of a federal court and Rob Sand, Iowa’s governor-elect, who won’t be sworn into office until January.

The Army had planned to detonate the barrels on November 20, but delayed the blast on Thursday amid public outcry and a legal challenge from environmental groups. The explosion will launch a plume of toxic gases and neurotoxic lead that could reach up to 100 miles away from the Iowa facility, the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant (IAAAP).

Iowa residents and officials said they learned of the detonation only days beforehand. The environmental groups, led by Earthjustice, claimed in an emergency court filing that the Army had not fully considered safer options for disposing of the lead azide before planning the detonation.

Late Thursday, a federal appeals court granted Earthjustice’s request to put a hold on the Army’s permit from the Environmental Protection Agency, which allowed for the controlled detonation to be carried out. Around the same time, Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle said the detonation would be postponed until Monday so the military could communicate with Iowans about the situation and plans.
Lead azide risk

Documents released by the Army last week said that the military first learned in March that the lead azide had started to degrade and crystallize. Lead azide is used in detonators for munitions, but in crystallized form it becomes highly unstable and sensitive to physical movement or friction. The IAAAP is said to contain around 9,700 pounds (4.4 tons) of lead azide in barrels held in earth-covered containers.

articles.headline: Deltarune Chapter 6 is playable "from the beginning to the end," Toby Fox says, but the RPG's final part has "only just started"
keyFacts: Deltarune creator Toby Fox announced that Chapter 6 is now a structurally complete draft playable from beginning to end.
Fox stated that the team still needs to complete localization, testing, and polishing before finishing the episode.
Fox reported that development on the final Chapter 7 has only just started with the team outlining its story and events.
body: Toby Fox has given eager fans an update on the development of Deltarune Chapter 6 and Chapter 7 - the Undertale follow-up's final two episodes.

"Chapte 6 is progressing well," he wrote in a new blog post. "The game is now a structurally complete draft that can be played from the beginning to the end. All the maps, events, and battles exist. (Although there's still one optional event which is dragging out a bit…)"

While the bones are supposedly all there, Fox explained that he and his team still need to knock out localisation, testing and polishing. "Much of the game looks complete… but, some important scenes and details are still undercooked in their presentation, so it's going to take a bit longer before we can really move to full-on testing."

Deltarune Chapter 6 was previously described as a slightly shorter episode that should hopefully set up the game's finale quite nicely. Despite being on the smaller side, Fox said he understandably doesn't want to rush development and "would like it to be as good as possible."
And since Deltarune's next chapter is almost past the finish line - at least, in some respect - that means certain members of the team have already moved over to Chapter 7.

"Well, we've only just started," Fox continued. "I read out the events and dialogue of Chapter 7 to the team. However, just when the story reached a critical moment, I stopped reading… I told my team they need to complete more of the game before I tell them what happens. Everyone agrees it's more fun this way"
"Unlike every other Chapter, I actually feel like I know what I'm doing this time, so I have a lot of confidence."

Deltarune's been on a long journey to get here, but, thankfully, the end is finally in sight. Deltarune debuted as a free download all the way back in 2018, a second chapter then dropped in 2021, the next two launched together four years later, before the arrival of the most recent Chapter 5 this year.

We don't know exactly how long Deltarune's last two chapters might take, but the good news is that it's already been a pretty fantastic game for years. Here's hoping those loose threads don't dangle for much longer.

articles.headline: 28 years later, grizzled XCOM-style WW2 tactics game Soldiers at War gets a fresh tour of duty on modern PCs
keyFacts: Publisher SNEG released a new version of the turn-based tactics game Soldiers at War for modern PCs.
The updated version includes compatibility improvements, widescreen resolution support, cloud saves, and achievements for modern systems.
The game features 18 main scenarios set during World War 2 where players control squads of eight soldiers.
body: Prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a new version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO Series, except that it's set during World War 2. I don't believe they had Chryssalids back then. Pretty sure grandpa never mentioned any Chryssalids.

Originally developed by Random Games and published by Strategic Simulations, Inc, the game consists of 18 main scenarios spanning D-Day, Monte Cassino and Cherbourg. There's a mission editor, too, and some standalone extra skirmishes. In each scrap, you pick eight men to undertake such feats as raiding V2 sites and hijacking disabled tanks, drawing on a pretty dizzying range of individual soldier actions. Your squaddies level up with experience, and you can equip them with flamethrowers and bazookas. Among the key differences from X-COM is that there's no morale system - your men will never defy orders. Nor is there an overarching base/Geoscape layer.

"This edition updates Soldiers at War to run smoothly on modern Windows systems, delivering improved compatibility and performance," promises the GOG page (it's also on Steam). "The game now supports 1280x720 widescreen resolution, with rendering improvements for smoother drawing." There are cloud saves and Achievements, too, for today's soldier is not content with merely laying down their life for their country. They must also unlock some percentage-based virtual trophies in the process.

I remember Strategic Simulations, Inc mostly for working on two games in the Close Combat series, but they developed and published a shedload of other strategy games and wargames before their eventual parent company Ubisoft retired the brand in the noughties. As for Random Games – hold the phone, those guys also made the original Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate!

articles.headline: James Talarico's Mom Shares Pic Of Sen.-Elect And Girlfriend That Breaks Internet
keyFacts: Tamara Talarico shared a photo of Texas Senator-Elect James Talarico and his girlfriend, Brianna Menard, at a football game.
Menard is Talarico's former chief of staff and a healthcare lobbyist who wore a thrifted dress in the photo.
Talarico was elected to the U.S. Senate after defeating Ken Paxton.
body: The mother of James Talarico shared a photo of the senator-elect from Texas and his girlfriend that has social media buzzing and some admirers gushing over one detail.

Talarico and Brianna Menard attended the University of Texas Longhorns’ 45-3 victory over the University of Arkansas in Austin on Saturday. Both are UT alums and proudly sported versions of the school’s burnt orange color.
But according to the Democrat’s mother, Tamara Talarico, Menard’s fashion choice was the true winner because she got her minidress at a thrift store.
“I love this picture of Jimmy and Brianna! My favorite part is she thrifted that dress last week!” the mother wrote.
While the hyper-viral post drew all kinds of comments from haters and supporters alike, several observers cheered Menard’s down-to-earth-sourced outfit.
Check out other reactions here:
The couple chatted with cheerleaders on the sideline and Talarico fired the traditional Smokey the Cannon, The Austin American-Statesman reported. He also participated in the pregame coin toss.
Menard was Talarico’s former chief of staff in his state House office and is now a healthcare lobbyist.
As conservatives ramped up accusations that he was gay, Talarico mentioned his girlfriend as his “rock” and “best friend” back in May, but did not give her name for privacy reasons.

Later in the campaign, his team told the New York Times,“Four years ago, after he and his then-chief of staff developed feelings for each other and started dating, she left the office to pursue other opportunities. As right-wing operatives continue to attack James’s loved ones, the campaign is asking the public to respect Brianna’s privacy as a private citizen.”
Talarico helped lead a Democratic takeover of the U.S. Senate with his victory over Trump-endorsed, scandal-plagued Ken Paxton.
